title: Mike LaFleur Press Conference 8.5.26 | AZ Cardinals
text: Well, of course, we've got to ask you, is uh is Jeremiah Love going to play tomorrow? What's the deal? >> Uh he will not be playing tomorrow. So, he'll uh today, just to give you guys some context on what today is, again, trying to be where your feet are. This is uh a practice. Uh so, the uh that first group will be out there. So, him and TA will will split. Um you know, once today, it's full speed, it's full padded. Um it's a practice for us. So, uh we'll get that quality work in and then um you know, moving forward, getting into that Vegas and then um the next week, that's when we'll uh we'll see those guys. >> How did your mind [snorts] take that whenever you talked to us? He was pretty intent about playing on Thursday. >> I don't know cuz I didn't have that talk with him. Cuz again, it's you know, it's um you know, in the message of being where your feet are, I wasn't really concerned about whether what they were I just wanted them, you know, worried about that practice and and going from there. So, um again, I I would say if we had all 90 guys said you guys were all up, they'd all be thrilled to play, I would hope cuz they love football. Um but that wasn't going to be the case for this game the whole the whole time. >> Do you know I imagine the list of guys who are not playing is is too long to list all them off, but do you know roughly how many guys I'm not going to make you sit here for 5 minutes doing that, but do you know roughly how many guys are are going to you're going to kind of avoid playing? >> Um six about 16 on offense and maybe double that, you know, maybe a tick more on defense. So, you're talking let's just say 35 guys out of the 90 right there. So, it's going to kind of have a resemblance in pregame and uh obviously the game of what a 53-man roster look like, you know, and obviously you got your guys that are down and stuff like that on game day, but it'll it'll have that kind of sideline, if you will. It won't feel like your your total 90-man roster in a preseason. >> As you head into [snorts] your first preseason game, what's the progress been like for the entire rookie class from the first day they showed up and do the facility up at training camp? >> Yeah, I would say just some improvement every single day. Um and uh and and you can see it. I think it it's been tangible and uh the comfort level and all that. And tomorrow we get the uh you know, pull the training wheels off. Uh there's no coaches behind them. There's no coaches prepping them Uh except for obviously when they come to the sideline and then you know, we'll coach them up and it'll be cool to see just a lot of these guys demeanors if you will, you know, when it when when it's real when the bullets are live again just cuz it's preseason and the win loss doesn't matter doesn't count doesn't mean that this isn't real football. I mean guys are fighting you know, their butts off to to make teams to put good product out there to put good tape out there and and compete. Whether it's the ping pong table or playing. I mean in that three and a half hour window Carolina is going to want to win a game just like we are. It doesn't count after the fact but in that moment I don't care what you're doing if you're competitor you care. >> Do you have different things that you're looking for from those rookies compared to a veteran tomorrow? >> Uh no, you know, just continued improvement continue moving the needle needle up like we we keep talking about. We don't we don't need a don't need a peak again tomorrow. We just need to keep continue to improve tomorrow. What's going to be different is again cuz it's live. I mean naturally the competition level's going to go up. >> Nick Allen said yesterday that Josh went despite not being able to practice he's been in meetings he's been like a really good leader for the team. What have you seen his role look like even though he can't be out there with his >> Yeah, it's it's what Nick said yesterday. I mean he's he's in all the meetings he's around he looks he looks again I know I've said it so broken record there but he looks really good in terms of healthy in shape all those kind of things. He's putting a lot of work in you know, behind the scenes to to make sure when you know, he gets the green light and everyone feels good and and ultimately making sure Josh feels good both mentally and physically to go out there and perform the way cuz he takes a lot of pride in what what his product looks like. That tape matters a lot to him as I've gotten to know him you know, so he's earned the right to to you know, communicate with us to say hey, I feel good. I'm I'm ready to go but again, I'm not whether you believe me or not I'm not I'm not worried about him come September 13th at all. >> It seems like the the last couple full speed practices you guys have had Marvin's gotten open a lot down field. What is what have you seen from him and and if you're seeing the same thing I'm seeing what's what's enabling that success? >> Yeah, well he's he's got a I'd say an interesting gate, you know, and and um you can stand out in front of him. I can stand out in front of him on a route and I mean that's a big dude coming at you and like all we talk about with Marvin initially is just that ball get off that urgency, that stance and start because when he's coming off and he's got that body lean, like I said it's it's it's weird for a defender, you know, and it's hard to explain but all you have to do is watch the final tape. It's like, you know, like how do you separate? Like it was that a good, you know, was I good at the top of my route? It's like, well watch the watch the defender. You tell me, you know, it's pretty easy right there, you know, to to know. So when we can get him some access and all those kind of things, you know, protect his route stem a little bit. He's got he's got great knowledge of like how all these routes play off of each other. Um and and doesn't say anything about it, you know, it's it's it's our job as coaches, my job to to make sure that we're protecting it but then his job to, you know, marry those kind of things up. So he's done a good job with it, you know, it was cool in that two-minute situation. I thought that was a great double move that he ran on on Burke and and Jacoby threw a great ball right there and and then it was on top of it a great learning lesson in terms of, you know, in that situation down to what we would have done after that for me and and for those players. >> When you say protect [snorts] his route stem, what do you mean by that? >> Make it sure that he, you know, we protect every angle of the cut. So at the top, you know, he can let's just say it's an 18 to 20-yard route, you know, you can you can spray that release, you can stop and go back to the quarterback, you can break out, you can break in, you can speed cut it or you can double move off of it or you can run the post off of it. So all those kind of all those, you know, all his stems, not just him, all these guys whether they're playing X, C, Y, F, it's like what do they do well and then let's make sure we have, you know, every angle out of that out of that stem. >> So you can make sure that they're in a position, schematically, where the cornerback can't eliminate things, where the cornerback can't be like, "Oh, this guy's not going to do this." >> That's exactly right. 100%. >> It [snorts] feels like receivers are always open during the practice. It's still very early. It hasn't been against live competition. Sure, you're keeping things vanilla for the guys, but how pleased have you been with the team's reception of this new new offense, how it's been installed, and like where it can possibly go? yeah, I'd say uh pleased would be strong, cuz I have high standards for these guys, but I've been very pleased with the way these guys attack it. Um and and and how they're trying to learn what they're doing in the meetings, uh what they do in jog-through, how it's very intentional and it's very deliberate, and how they attack practice. I've been pleased with the play style, albeit we haven't tackled, and we we don't know what it looks like on Sunday. So, we got a long way to go, or what it's going to look like on Sundays. But, uh you know, these guys they they know we got a long ways. Uh you know, both schematically and and um just foundationally and fundamentally uh to get to where we want to get to on September 13th. >> We were just [snorts] talking about I feel like your defensive line and your first-team defensive line is wreaking a lot of havoc out there in practice, but it's That's a really hard thing from the sideline to kind of know like who is responsible for for creating that havoc. Who have some of the guys been that have made that happen? >> I I Yeah, I'm not even going to mention any names, because I think you said it like it's it's it's been a lot of those guys. And it it What's great about on defense is one guy can can uh have a quick win, and it can just totally derail the offensive play, whether it's the run or the pass game. So, um I I think that whole unit has done a good job in you know, in picking and choosing which guy it's going to be each time. So, um we're going to go as about as far on this defense as our D-line takes us. Point-blank period. And in all in all phases, first, second, and third down. And uh I've liked what we saw, but again, just like we just said with the offense, we got a long way to go. >> Uh James and Trey Benson in the running backs field, they've they've been doing in some individual drills. Benson's a little bit more with the first team. Do you think either of them just obviously not going to be too involved, but do you think either of them are going to play in the preseason? Do you think they'll be ready for week one >> Uh I'm I'll hold off on that right now. I mean, in terms of you know, we're taking Trey day-by-day right now and and and James day-by-day, you know, and again James being in this league as long as he have and in the miles that he's put on. Um if James wants to play in the preseason to see where he's at, uh great. If he doesn't think that's necessary, great. And and again, I I I Um he he reserves the right to to have those conversations cuz he knows where his body's at. >> It's been a week and change now that Jacoby's been back. What do you What have you seen from him? >> Yeah, continued improvement. Continued uh every day getting just a little bit more comfortable. Um it's great in terms of uh the way that we install and the amount of meeting times. They get with Shobby and Hack, able to you know, preview the script, really review the day before, all those kind of things, preview the script. Uh then we go install in front of the unit, and then we do a stage walk-through, so now we're on you know, the third time he's heard it by the time he's even eaten had lunch. Then you you're able to go walk through it, so now it's the fourth time he's called it, and then the fifth time ends up being at 4:00 in those practices. Today being a little accelerated for obvious reasons with the travel and all that. So, what do we do? We just did that last night. You know, he got the script. I went into the quarterback room, we talked about all 24 plays he's going to have today. Talk about why we're doing it, what the intent is. Um and then we'll be able to go walk through it in kind of an accelerated fashion, they'll be able to go call it. So, just the comfort level for him. Again, the concepts are the concepts. He's basically ran all these at some point in his career. Um called some things in the walk-through for our defense yesterday, some empty type stuff, so our defense was getting their alerts and cans. And you know, he looked at me on one of them, I said, "New England 2016." He goes, "Oh, okay, good." You know, and he knew exactly what we were talking about right there. So, our 17, whatever it was. So, um yeah, no, it's it's it's it's going good one day at a time. >> What do you think has surprised you about being an NFL head coach so far? You've been in this seat for a couple months now. You've been around a lot of really great NFL head coaches, but obviously you can't replicate that till you get in the seat yourself. Has there been anything big or small that's kind of made you go, "Man, like I didn't really think about that until I was a head coach." you never assume anything, but but again, I I kind of I kind of went with that. So, this one this one's always hard for me because it's like you just try to take it day by day. I think if you'd asked me this last night when you're really reflecting and my mind's not really just focused on getting out there at 9:00 for this walk-through, I probably had something for you, but the the answer I keep going to is just, you know, when when you get asked what color markers you want for your board and where the boards go. It's like put the board on the wall and give me the markers that work. Like Like what are we talking about, you know? Like keep the main thing the main thing. It's football. But again, you you do have those things that come across your desk and and you have to roll with it. >> Do you have a message to the team before you guys break for camp? >> Uh yeah, handled today and then we'll talk tomorrow.

Uh, and the sneaky guy a lot of people don't know why I take a lot of my game from is Jordan Norwood. Um, but those guys, I had Benny Fowler. I mean, there's just a lot of a lot of guys that were showing me the ropes early on. And then I got Odell back when I was in with New York. So, um, a lot of guys helping me. And then through those trials and tribulations, I learned that this game is very, very, very hard. So, um, why not give back to swap see somebody else who can kind of skip the stuff that you kind of had to go through the valleys for? So, >> Zavon said, uh, on his first day here, Ben told him to just follow you. >> Oh, [laughter] yeah. >> What's that process been like? Is he following you, >> dude? No, that that guy is a along [snorts] with being incredibly talented, um, he is a sponge. Um, and he uh, dude, I'm so I'm so excited for who he is and who he's gonna be. Um, but most important, this is the coolest thing I say uh, two nights ago. He said, "Leaf, I got like a little ankle thing I do." He's I'm going to send you this video, the ankle stuff I do every night. He sent me a video. So, the ankles he doing every night in the back. I'm looking at the videos. I'm like, "One, I need to get on this. No wonder you're so fast." But two, um, is this kind of mentality that kind of creates that consistency, that discipline, that longevity, that will to be great later on. and he's doing it now every night. And um it's so cool just to watch something as simple as that, how it can transition over to no wonder he's fast, no wonder he's so disciplined, no wonder he's so eager because something as small as that he's thinking every night. Um it's a sign of maturity. So >> what was he doing? What specifically was he doing? Oh man, it's it's like ankle mobility like just toe to toe stretches anterior tip for like you know kid which helps the knees and ankles but uh it's just it's it's it's a small thing that ends up paying off over time cuz uh every night I mean you go two weeks in that's 14 days of ankle stability and stretching but uh it takes it's a vet type mindset to to be as disciplined to do something like that. And when he showed me that video I was just I was just happy to know like that's who he is. So it's awesome. personally figured [clears throat] out ways to keep more speed out here as you get older. >> Yeah. Yeah. Yeah. I got a couple couple couple secrets. Uh I uh the stretching every night uh helps. And then uh um if I give out too much secrets there is cuz some of the stuff sound real old [laughter] like metabolism stuff. But uh one thing I did that did help me is uh I try to touch top speed at least once a week. Uh just cuz you rev your engine up. Um, if you are going 60% bend in the corner on a punt return, but you touch your touch touch your top speed, your range goes from like here to like here. So, like you can get that. So, that kind of helped reverse the world of time a little bit because now I have access to all of it versus I'm only hitting here during the week. So, >> the other day I was talking to after practice. I was waiting for you and I I swear you caught 200 from the jugs machine. >> Uhhuh. >> Where did you learn that? Why is that important to you? And was I correct in my count? >> No, that's perfect. Yeah, it's 205 and it's only 205 cuz that knucklehead in Detroit is getting 202 every day. Uh, and he hate miss. So, and that's three time all pro and I know he's on the other side now, but there something you can learn from it. So, uh, I watch him go 202 every day. I've never seen a miss and if he didn't see it after cuz he got it before. So, in my head, if he getting 202 one and he all pro, you need to be touching it. But two, he ain't beating me. So, that's why I got the 205. >> 205. >> No, he knows. He knows. He knows the the the issue is not getting 205 one day. is getting it every single day that we're out there. Um, so that's where the discipline comes in. So I'm trying to be that tier. Um, and um, get on that level of discipline and hard work. So 205 is where we at and my hands will not like me for it. So yeah, >> interested to know your feelings about the organization prior to joining the Bears as an outsider looking in. How did you feel about this team? And now that you're here, uh, what are your feelings about the culture? >> Oh, goodness. First off, you shot that out the dark coming after that. That was crazy. Um, >> from the tribe. >> Um, no man, um, very appreciative. You can tell at least from a special team perspective how how these guys play, but as a team, as organization and, uh, one of the coolest part and I mentioned history when I first got here. I don't know if y'all been to that room that's over there like by our team meeting room. And then you just looking around and you're seeing the names that come with it. So, um, my dad will always be like the 85. He used to play that on. So, like, so like it's there's a lot of nostalgia coming out here. Um, but more importantly, when I got here, I could feel the they said last year's team was as tight as as a lot of teams in the NFL you can see. And being amongst the guys in here, um, I'm getting that same feel. Like, no wonder, man, we got a high character guys. Um, high efficiency with high work ethic. Um, the amount of DBs right now catching jugs is crazy to me. U, but the will to work, the will to be better. I can sense how this team was so close-knit last year and uh we're trying to replicate that as much as we can because uh this group right here is just as impressive. So, >> how Khif, how have you seen Ben Johnson evolve as a uh play caller, play schemer? And then is he asking you to do similar things to Detroit? >> Um I think the cool thing about Ben is he's always evolving. like there isn't Ben has such um a unique way of looking at the game and looking at play schemes and all that stuff. Um and I think it's not a matter of how far Ben can evolve, but a matter of how much can we he trusts his guys to go out there and execute all the things. And that's uh that's a lot to do with us too, being able to be detailed and all the stuff that we're doing. Um I think the coolest part about Ben is just watching him become a leader of of men. um because it's not just one side of the ball when you when you get to the game, it's it's three phases of football. So, watching him adapt, uh watching him and DA's connection, watching him HT's connection where he's watching the things he's looking at, how the this ST drill translates over to the game, how translated over to practice. So, watching him being a leader of men is uh really cool because it's a lot of when he walks in the room, man, he he he commands respect. Um and you know that he has your your best your best intention at heart. Do you sense that he and Caleb are very much on the same page? I mean, that Caleb is kind of echoing what he's saying. >> Yeah. No, no, it's it's it's uh I think you'll notice uh their relationship cuz I can't like I said, I can't speak on it, but it's the little moments like in between uh what time Caleb gets the call. He kind of has like they have like a little one, two before he gets to the huddle. Um so that's my been my like close experience of watching their connection. Um you can tell they're kind of like bouncing off words and ideas that's coming next. So, um, that's been pretty cool. It's just it's it's like 5 seconds and if you're not paying attention, you won't see it, but it's just watching them kind of go back and forth of what they're thinking, how they're seeing it. Um, it's been really cool to watch that develop. So far, >> where do you think the uh offense is at right now? >> Um, I think we are in the foundation phase [laughter] just because of where we are where we are in camp, man. You're still uh you're trying to develop consistency and trust. You know, we got call up periods where like there ain't there ain't no script. You just letting it go. And you got like eight installs right now. So you just you calling it. We called a play today and uh I looked at Lou. Lou looked at me and then we're like Lou told me he got that's how I knew what I got and that's why I know what he got. So just that level of trust through eight installs. We're in the foundation where we're like, "Hey man, it's a caller period. I can throw anything at you guys. You guys go handle it." So we're in the foundation period and that's where we're trying to find some growth. So >> how would you evaluate the speed of the defense? That was one of the things that was talked about coming in. I figure one of the fastest players on the team would be able to evaluate it best. >> Oh man, one of the fast players on the team. That's uh And you want me to evaluate the defense, huh? That's crazy. I know. What was really cool is uh otaas. So Caleb Scrim I I think Caleb Scrim somebody scramble was to the right. Could have been a quarterback. I don't know. I think it was a quarterback and D Bush. I said, "Oh, who is that?" Cuz that was could have been a sack in the game. So, um that's just one instance. I was like, man, I don't know who that linebacker is, but you know, he you break a chain. You better watch that joker right there cuz he's coming. So, um that was one of the cool moments. Um but no, we got a lot of guys who who can move. Uh, and it's we're bouncing around who who we put on the 4x1 team right now and it's a couple of defensive guys are going to be on there. So, um, no, we're pretty fast. So, >> last one, Chris. >> Thanks, Cal. Uh, Khiv Ben talked to us last week talking about this is the number one regression candidate in the league. I'm sure he said something similar to you guys and talking about you guys coming off the season you had last year. >> How does he harp on these things, the motivational tactic, and how similar is that to what Dan would do in Detroit, >> the number one regression candidate? >> Yeah. talking about the record you guys had last year and what people on the outside are saying and how similar has Ben to to Dan in terms of building that motivational edge and using that kind of thing to get you guys going. >> Um I the cool part is Ben isn't harping on last year. He's like, "Hey man, there is a there is a standard that good teams have. Not standard from last year, not he said there's a standard that when you watch a team that's good. This is what they do. This is how they operate. This is how they practice. This is the level of intensity they are." He said this is what good teams do. So that standard is what he preaches. He doesn't preach, hey, don't fall into the trap. He's like, hey man, there's a standard no matter where you see it is a standard that good teams have and this is what we have to attain every time we step out on the field. That's what he's preaching to us. So it doesn't matter what what's going on where we're good in this phase like that. He's like either way, it's a standard that when we step on the field, that's what we need to hit. So everybody has a one track mind. We got to meet that standard every day. So that's where we are. >> Austin, how would you maybe describe the physicality of today's practice? >> Uh super physical. I mean, that's what we've been doing every day. So, um, that's what we're getting used to. That's how we're going to play this year. So, we got to, uh, we got to make it look like that in practice. Do >> you feel like it maybe ramped up today versus other days or is it just a thing where pads are back on? >> No, I just think pads are back on and that's how we have to play every I mean, every snap. We're aggressive. So, >> you got you got tangled with Braxton one on. What did you see? Obviously, he was uncomfortable afterwards. >> I mean, I didn't see too much. I'm kind of just doing my thing, you know, obviously that's my brother, so um hearts with him, but um we're just competing every day and hearts follow what they do. >> So, what did you work on over the offseason where that you can now finally employ that in padded practices? >> Um lower body strength, uh my get off um all those combined just getting stronger faster every year. I know people are going to ask you about pass rush, but how much pride do you take in a play like you made at the end there when you go in the back field and drop the running back? >> Yeah, I mean it's obviously getting a sack's great, but getting a TFL is even better. I mean, you have to work even harder for it. So, um just getting off being aggressive at the point of contact, um that's been a big emphasis this year. >> We don't usually see the nine verse seven and 9 vers9 like those run game drills like what is that? Do defensive players like that? do. >> Yeah, we I mean, shoot, we love it. I mean, that's that's that's our that's our mentality this year. We're getting off the ball. We're being aggressive at blocks um and getting in the back field. So, >> what's been your approach coming into this season knowing that the Bears uh didn't go get any bigname edge rushers or uh a whole lot of free agents and and the fact that it seems like they're they have confidence that you can hold it down there. Yeah, I mean I'm blessed for the opportunity for sure. Um but I mean my mentality is the same as every year. Um I'm going to get better and I'm going to do my part as best as I can. So um yeah, >> I know you started the season a little later last year, but it felt like you really came on there towards the end. Like what was the key for you hitting your stride? [snorts] >> Just shoot. I mean, I got I got took I got taken out obviously and I came back with the same mentality I have every year is to make plays and do as much as I can to for the team to win. So, >> Austin, there's a whirlwind of emotion surrounding this team after last year's success. How do you guys stay focused? >> Uh, day by day. Uh, you get better every day. Um, we improve every day and that's what camp's about, the long days. So, we're we're about to go into meetings and and clean up the practice and then we going to get better tomorrow. So, >> Austin, what was your what was your process for improving your get off? >> Uh, I mean, at first it was bulky. Um, two foot pushing. Um, a better stance, more loaded in my stance. Um, yeah. >> What have you seen from Jordan Vandenberg and the intensity he brings as a rookie? >> Yeah, he's a dog. I love playing with him. Um, I I have super high standards for him because how hard he works. Um, and I think we all see it on the field that he's a really good player. So >> when Montes comes off today, is there any notion that okay, everybody's got to step up in their reps then? >> Um, no. That that should be always that should always be the notion like next man up like you should be ready regardless whether he's practicing the full practice or whether he doesn't practice at all like next next man up for sure. >> What does it do for the overall confidence of your unit having Dio back? >> I mean it's been great. Uh that was a big piece from last year. Um, and we know we have someone we can rely on on the on the on the edge. So, >> we saw him kick inside too, especially in two-minute. What does that how do you feel like that combination helps the defensive line? It's like Hardy on one side today. Hardy, him, and then you're on the other side, too. >> Yeah, I think it adds some speed to the to the line and we're just going to uh maybe mix a couple things up and and see what works for us. So, >> is this the most back and forth that you've seen in your couple years here during camp? Seems like you guys go out and you win a few team drills, the offense comes out and they find a way to adjust and you guys are kind of having a good back and forth there. >> Yeah, definitely. It's great competition and uh we're blessed to have the offense we have and I know the offense feels the same about us. So, uh we just got to compliment each other this year and I think we we all see that. Um so, yeah. >> What kind of strength or weight training did you focus on this off season? >> Uh I mean the normal stuff, but at the same time I like to do sled pushes at the end of every workout. Um, that's really helped my my lower body. So, >> are you still a 245 or you >> I mean I'm 250 250 son. So, >> how y'all doing? >> Good. How's the adjustment been to uh getting out there playing a little more safety? >> Uh, it's been good uh so far. So, uh just doing a little bit more walkthrough stuff. You know, at first I was just splitting time from nickel and safety and a little uh portion at dime as well. So trying to learn everything, but uh you know what happened with Kobe a couple days ago. Got told to focus a little bit more on safety. So just been studying that. So it's it's been going good. I've been playing safety for say like four or five years now. So uh I like the position, but you know just learning the defense here, the communication, running the show back there, just getting adjusted to it. >> What's the biggest difference between being up at the nickel and and being back there at s? >> A lot a lot of things happen faster, you know, in the nickel run fits. um playing a lot of press man to man. Um but you know on the back end you just communicator of the defense uh you get a chance to see every kind of like everything routes develop and uh looking at different concepts and stuff like that and and just coming down here and breaking on the ball. >> How do you stay dialed into both spots cuz theoretically you playing safety would be temporary and then Kobe comes back and then you would be needed at different places. Yeah, it's um I've been doing like um I guess cross trainining you would say um for a little bit of time now. Honestly, my whole career. Um try to get a grasp of the whole defense as a whole and and the concept teaching um how they want different, you know, positions to play it. So, um say if it's a linebacker and we're playing cover three, how they play cover three for like a curl flag would be the same thing as a nickel. So just understanding the concept as that and um turning my brain off was like okay I'm not playing safety now I'm playing nickel let's focus on nickel okay I'm going back to safety let's turn the safety brain on so it takes it's a little adjustment especially you know with the new system you know coming from Buffalo but um been putting in the work you know you got to put in extra work uh study a lot uh just to make sure you just understand what they're asking you to do >> what is the grasp [clears throat] for you to grasp from a defense like that where you don't have to start thinking about it are you're at that point or is it still a process? >> It's still a process. Uh it's still early. Um I didn't have a chance to really practice too much in the spring. Um so I felt like I'm a little bit behind the Aball when it comes to that. Really just getting the reps and repetitions, but that's really all it comes down to is just reps. Um just yeah, just getting to feel and custom comfortable to the defense. So the more reps I get, the more comfortable I get. So by the time the season come around, I should be more than comfortable. I was going to ask is is that the biggest challenge like getting more comfortable in the system or is there like the reading recognition part of the position? That's the challenge. >> I feel like it's comfortable like playing safety is playing safety I feel like anywhere. Uh but really like I said just understanding the system and what they asking you to do in that system and then uh the communication aspect and once you get it then you're able to go out there and play football uh you know play the game that you've been playing since you were a little kid. Just go out there and fly around. That's when it when the games get simpler, you know, a lot slower, but um until you under get that understanding, it's a it's still a little fast, you know what I'm saying? It it takes a little bit, but like I said, the reps are helping me out, walk through reps, um practice reps, full speed reps. So, um I'm getting it. >> How's it going partnering with Bill and just getting up speed? It's kind of him being a rookie and then you're just sliding in newer to the position at least here. Yeah, just uh daily talking to him. Um getting on the same page how he see things, how I see things. Um yeah, honestly just the same page things, you know, still early in camp. Uh haven't had a lot of reps with him so far, so just still kind of getting adjusted to him. But uh he's a hell of a player. I'm excited for him and see what he does in his career. But um yeah, just just getting comfortable with each other. just communication, talking after um when we doing walkthroughs, see what he sees right here, how we can hold different disguises and stuff like that. So, uh we got a lot of room to grow. It's still early, but I'm excited for that. >> You've been in the deep, you've been in the NFL since 2019. You've obviously seen a lot more offenses than than he has knowing what these looks are. much of it the onus is on a veteran player when you have a rookie who's playing opposite you of like handling the communication making sure he sees something that he might not recognize initially but that's you know something you've obviously seen before. I mean, um, yes, that's a big thing. Uh, just from my experiences, you know, relaying all the stuff that helped me, you know, pick up different offenses, different concepts, but a lot of stuff, we really take a look at it. A lot of teams run the same thing. They just dress it up and hide it up just a little bit different with a little bit of motions in here. And once you understand that, and once you understand what how they're trying to scheme you, your weakness of your defense, um, it makes it a little bit easier to play defense. Um, but on the communication aspect, he's been on it. Like I like he's really been on it. He's been in his playbook. So, kudos to him. Uh, we need that, especially him feeling in a strong safety. And, um, yeah, I'm just, like I said, I'm just excited for him to watch him grow. But, um, sometimes he may see something and he tell me, "Oh, got this." And I need that, you know, cuz I'm not perfect. I can't see everything. And the same thing goes for me. If I see something, I'm I'm letting him know. So, we're just working with with each other. Uh we're not out there alone. It's a it's a unit back there. So, uh just holding each other accountable. >> On [clears throat] the field, what what jumps out about Dylan for you? >> Instinctive, fast, um not afraid to, you know, stick his nose in there. Um I feel like he's a natural bone playmaker. So, I'm excited to see what he do, especially, you know, this preseason and this season. >> How the defense performed today, especially after that that first 90 N7 session, it seemed like you got >> Hard to tell. I mean, 907 I feel like went pretty well. Um, first team period, the live period, we didn't start how we wanted to start. You know, they scored on the first play, so that's never good. But I feel like we bounce back throughout the day, but uh it's hard to give you um a good answer right now without watching the tape, you know. Um it's never as good as we think, it's never as bad as we think. So, it may be somewhere in the middle. What stressed you? >> You're obviously part of a program [clears throat] that figured out how to be successful and stay successful. What did you learn about the wheels that keep that thing moving? >> Um, just [sighs] a lot of stuff is like player le honestly. Um, Buffalo Mcderman just gave the guys the keys like what you guys want to be like what type of team do you guys want to be and the type of culture. Uh, everybody didn't want to let their brother down and everybody was fighting for the same goal, you know, trying to win a championship. So, um, and Buffalo was just a little bit different, too. It's not like really a major major city. So, it wasn't a lot to do outside of work. Uh, so everybody, you know, hung out with each other, you know, everybody was barbecues over at each other house. The DBs used to do uh DB dinners every Thursday. So to [snorts] have that um camaraderie all the time, you know, even when we're not on the field, makes you uh want to play for your brother makes you not want to uh mess up for him, you know, uh we all got each other's back. So I think that's what we're trying to do here as well. You know, make sure just knit the group together, you know, offense and defense and and special teams, you know, everybody has a role to play. Um if everybody does their job, we should be all right. What has struck you the last four months about what you joined here and what the foundation is that you walked into? >> Honestly, the same thing. Uh, you know, you tell Ben wants to win. He wants to score points and then, you know, DA wants the offense to fear you and that's how you're supposed to, you know, play defense. Um, I like it so far. You know, we still haven't we have been through a little bit adversity so far. So depending on how we uh looking, you know, bounce back from that, but uh it's a lot. You know, we still got to grow. Still early. Got a long season to go. So, it's going to be a lot of ups and downs, but the closer this group gets together, the better we'll be. >> K, what did you learn? >> I mean, you said DA wants an offense to to fear you. What gives you that impression? What's what struck you about DA so far? >> He's very passionate about, you know, his defense, and I think that's what you want out of defensive coordinator. You don't want a defensive coordinator to be passive, you know, soft. He wants to attack. Um, and that's what you want in this league. You want teams to defer your defense. Like, oh, we got Chicago on the schedule. It's going to be a headache type of game. You know, their defensive line going to come off the ball. The DB is going to break on the ball. Our linebackers going to play downhill and uh make some plays. So, that's that's the type of defense we want. And that's the type of defense we're striving to be. Like I said, we just ped a long way to go, you know. Um, but if we're trying to get better each and every day, that's step closer to our goal. >> Cam, when you were in Buffalo and you had to step in and start, you know, did last year in the playoffs and did throughout your career. What did you learn from those experiences to Monday when Kobe gets hurt and just kind of rewire and be like, "All right, this is my job now. I got to I got to do this." >> Always be ready. You know, you never know when your opportunity is going to come. Um, but when it comes, you got to make the most of it. So it's like, you know, I for example, I was like, you know, preparing for games. I was playing, you know, backup nickel and our safety gets hurt. Now I got to go play safety. So um it takes a lot, you know, on the mental side to learn both or prepare for both a week to week standpoint, but you just got to be ready to go out there and play and can't be afraid to make mistakes, you know, because I am going to make mistakes out there. I'm not perfect. Nobody on this defense or this team is perfect, but just go out there and fly around. Have fun doing it and you should be all right in there. >> What kind of perspective as a player from your seasons in Buffalo do you think you bring or maybe the strengths you want to hone into in an expanded role now? >> Um that I'm honestly I'm not a selfish guy. I'm a team guy. I play wherever you need me to play. Um I always been that way, you know, growing up. Uh, football is a great team sport and I love it so much just because it's not individual based, you know. Um, that's why, you know, I can play safety. I can go and play nickel. I can go play diamond if you need me to and go play special teams. It's like it's not about me. Um, I'm playing for the whole whole team, the whole city, and just trying to go out there and do my best. That's that's the only thing I can do.

title: Ben Johnson looking for execution and growth | Press Conference
text: few things that popped up since since last time I was up here. Obviously Kobe went down with the injury. We're still in a in an information collection phase on that. Um in terms of the timeline and and the extent of it, we should have more information here uh within the next few days though. Um it was good to have TJ back out there yesterday. Uh we'll continue to get him more involved and ramped up. You could certainly feel his presence and hear his communication out there on the on the defense, which was good to see. Uh, and then of course we had Darnell Wright and his contract extension got announced. Um, proud of Darnell, all the hard work that he's put in. He's really earned it and uh, it's a credit to him and and the people around him to make that happen. So, with that, I'll go ahead and open it up. >> Today's the uh, eighth practice of camp. Where are things at with Kylo Gordon and is there any update? >> There there's no update. We're just continuing to rehab. with with Darnell, what are what's something other players, especially younger players, can kind of learn from watching him and get that contract working together? >> Well, I mean, I think it's it's a prime example that potential and talent gets you into a building, but then how you work, you go about your business, um how you grow every single day, that that's what gets you um a long-term contract like he's got right now. You know, he's he's really embraced what we're trying to build here. Um, you know, I I've been in here for for a year and a half and I don't know if I've seen a guy improve as much as him. Um, just more so from a consistency standpoint than anything else. I mean, he's always had it in him uh in flashes, but the way he played a year ago, um, it was no secret that that we really relied on that right side of the offensive line for our run game engine to go and, uh, and he was a huge part of that. and the way he's attacked this off seasonason, what he's looked like so far in camp. Um, I think the future's really bright for him. So, that's the that's the message that that the young guys get. >> Was talking yesterday expressing gratitude about everybody in the building was kind of invested in him and and [clears throat] he he pointed to you when he said that you instilled that he's going to be part of this offense. What What was your kind of thought about your approach with him and making him known that he's a key part of what you're doing? Well, I didn't know him very well obviously, but um I I loved him coming out of Tennessee and so when you when you have that, you know, every player that comes through the draft, you kind of have a vision for and and how you could utilize them and use them and um and so I was excited to get that going and and uh you know, like I said, it took everybody in the building. It's it's Ryan, it's Dan Roshark, Kyle De Van, it's it's everybody helping that vision come along for him and what he can be. And I I think he's still on the on a upward trajectory. It it is not he has not arrived by any stretch of the imagination. There there's still more layers to Darnell Wright as a player that that we're looking to peel back. How have you seen his play speed and what translates from the the 40 time to to how he play? >> Yeah. Yeah. I mean it's funny. Um someone made a comment to me from Tuesday's practice or that that looked like his organ tape. The practice on Tuesday that looked like his organ tape and and it's hard to say that. Yeah. I mean it's it was our second day in pads. Um, but you can see that play speed start to show up. He is thinking a lot. And you know, the way he's wired is he wants to be on every little thing. And so when you're when you are like that, you you can potentially in your quest to be right every time, slow down and um, you know, it's just a matter of getting enough reps to where he can let loose and and get after it. I think Al Harris and and Matt Girardano are they're doing a phenomenal job getting them up to speed and um you know we're only a week week and a half into it right now. We have a long ways to go but um really like where he's at right now please. >> Seems like every uh receiver who's walked in here has mentioned Khalif Raymond and veteran presence. I know you have past experience with him but what >> what do you appreciate appreciate about what he's bringing to that room? >> Yeah, I mean he's he's everything that we thought um he was going to be. I mean, Ellen, I know him really well, obviously. Uh, and the work ethic, uh, the story behind the man. Um, just to hear how he had to fight, scratch, and claw to get to where he is today. Um, been cut multiple times and and yet still one of the elite punt returners in this game. Um, and and I mean, he's he's going to make a difference on our offense as well. He's got elite speed. He can do things after the catch. Um I I I just think he's a great role model for all those guys. It it really doesn't matter what position you're playing. Certainly in that room, he's made an impact, but I think throughout the offense, special teams unit, and the defense sees it as well. You know, I asking some of those defensive guys, um you know, if we had a 4x1 team here, who would they pick? And and Khif's the first one because his play speed is just off the charts and so um he's made a significant impact so far. >> Last three, Dion, Cord. Okay, so that was my question, but I'm going to pivot a little bit. We're also going to talk to Austin Booker today. What have you kind of seen from him as he comes into a very important camp trying to make his place up front? >> Yeah. Well, I mean, we've been talking a lot about the techniques and fundamentals that we're coaching on the defensive line. And we see that come to fruition now that we have the pads on. And so, it's the consistency of that play, the pad level, the hand usage. Um, you know, our defensive ends, they toggle between a nine technique and a six eye. And so there's there's different techniques that go along with it and along and so we need to see consistency of play in all of our edge players. And so that's what we're working through right now. Um that's where these padded practices are so so valuable. And that's why I get upset when the offense is are sabotaging practice a little bit because our defensive players need need these reps as much as anything else. But he's he's approached this off the offseason really well. Like what he looks like from a a body standpoint. when you're longlegged like that, it's a little bit lower or harder to get low in your stance. DA is still installing his defense schemes right now. We're still installing offensive schemes. There's a lot of learning going on and as we go through camp, we'll come to a consensus on the players we can count on the most, who the starters are going to be, what role they're going to play, and whether we need to adjust things schematically for us to have the most success on the field. It's going to happen to every team throughout camp and throughout the season. Um, we're no different than that. And um I've been asking different play callers across the league about their methodology during sort of the 25 seconds that you have per play. So I wonder what what you think about when you're trying to communicate with Caleb and maybe particularly in in two-minute or crunch time situations. Um whether there's what you do to maximize, you know, that that 25 seconds. Yeah, I mean I try to uh I try to get him to play as fast as I possibly can so that it gives him the maximum amount of time to communicate to his guys. Um recall the coaching points that we've already talked about. There's not a whole lot of extra dialogue unless it is one of those critical situations and we feel like, hey, this ball either needs to go uh out of bounds or incomplete, things of that nature might come up. But um for the most part, all of our conversations have taken place over the course of the week or the night before the game to where it's just a matter of how quickly can I get him the personnel and the play call so that he can go out there and and cut it loose like we talked about. But um I think it's worked out well. I think he really likes the communication aspect of it, but I'm not one of those guys that's in their ear all the way down to that that 50 15 second, you know, cut off time. So, um, which I I've been around guys they they've been around that and they're like, "Ah, [snorts] just shut up. I got it. I got this." So, they put in the work through the week and and we trust them on game day. >> Sorry. Yeah. So, after I've talked to some of the quarterbacks, too, and and the minimalist coaches when the communication is pre-established. They know the why. They know why. They sometimes know the play that's coming in before it's finished. Do you feel like you're there with Caleb where he's understanding it for that? >> Yeah, I don't know that we were there to start the season last year. I thought we got a lot closer as the year went. Um, you know, we spent a lot of time throughout the week just one-on-one making sure that we are aligned that way. Uh, I I do think that's where the best ones uh end up. So, we're on a quest to get there. >> Thank you. Thank you.
