title: Cowboys Players Honor Military Families & More | Player Interviews
text: Terrence, how special is this heroes appreciation meal? >> Oh, this is awesome. Um, you know, growing up a military brat myself, anytime we can, you know, celebrate the men and women who sacrificed and [snorts] uh, you know, put down their lives for this country, um, obviously want to celebrate that. So, it's a very, very special day for me. >> How do you like the physicality of these practices so far? I know Shotty talked about that's something you would like to see more out of of this group. >> Yeah. No, it's huge. Um, you know, especially for us in the trenches, O line, Dline, you know, physicality, that's the name of the game. That's who we are. That's in our identity. So, um, yeah, it's got to come out every time we put pads on. >> How excited are you to for that scrimmage next week to kind of figure out, okay, this is see what we got. >> Yeah. No, the Rams are obviously a great squad. Um, their defense is amazing. Um, yeah, just looking I'm excited for the challenge. You know, compete every day is our mantra. So, it's just another day to compete. >> How much have you monitored what they have done? I think Aaron Donald might be ready to go at some point to see what Washington's doing too with the digs. When you look at the opponents and what they've upgraded, do you follow that at all? >> Uh, to be honest, not really. Um, if I'm scrolling on Twitter or something, I'll see it. I don't I don't really give it too much thought to be honest with you. Um, I'm really just focused on what we got going on here, my job. Um, know my unit. So, um, I don't know. We'll just see when that when that day comes. >> You're a veteran. Can you still relate to the younger guys trying to make it and show what they have? >> Thousand%. Um, you know, just just going undrafted and having that chip on your shoulder and just trying to prove yourself, you know, every day. Uh, I can definitely relate to that and trying to give those young guys advice and just was successful for me and just trying to spread that knowledge. >> How do you think Giden has handled everything, you know, especially with a little competition >> like a pro, like a true pro. Um, you know, he could have diff he could have went a different way about it and obviously he did it he did the right way, you know. Um, I was with him a lot this offseason. Put a lot of great work in. Um, dude works his butt off. Um, so he came up in this this camp confident and it was on display. So we're very proud of him. Very very proud of him. >> Where has Tyler Brook made his biggest jump? We hear a lot about that. A guy going into a second year and having a full off season. >> I think just his knowledge of the game. Um, you know, he obviously saw a lot his first year. um just you know hearing about how he's talking about things now just whether it's between um know our B blocks just different leverages um progressing in the past pro game uh I think just his knowledge of the game has has taken a big jump and obviously he's a very physical guy um that's one of his great attributes and that's that's also continued to grow. >> What's been the biggest difference you've seen from these past rushers? They're in a [snorts] new scheme and what stands out to you when you face them now versus last year? Yeah. No, they're very very talented group obviously. Um very deep. Uh you know, they got BT. Uh he's he's done a great job coaching those guys up and they there's they're just very relentless in my in my opinion. Um they're not going to stop to the echo of the whistle and yeah, just just relentless group. >> Anything different in how they rush or any approaches that you see? >> Probably come with a little bit more power. That's sad to say. Yeah. >> Thank you very much for the time. course, >> you know, kind of get the scheme a lot more. Obviously, we're what, second week in the camp almost, uh, it's just about repetition at this point now, you know, building it, finally starting to put it all together. And, you know, we got a lot of young guys. I mean, I can say right now that's just playing their butts off right now, making plays, and that's what makes the team so special for us. Not only the the old guys making the plays and the communication stuff, but you could take the old guys out, you can put the young guys out there, and they'll be just as good. So, it's special to see. Speaking of communication, he talked about he talked to us yesterday talking about how loud the meeting room is like trying to figure you talk about that meeting room. What's it like in there? Uh the noise and all the talking communication that mirror >> man it's like how we are on the field man. You know like we always say the super bowl is the standard where we want to be and you know the the great that won the Super Bowls you know that's what it took for them to be that great. So we try to practice emphasize the same way in the meeting room as if we out here on film. I mean, out here on the field just for guys to hear the communication and know where guys is going to be at. And as you see, like I said, it's been playing off for us. You know, we've been playing playing well in uh practices against the offense. And like I said, the offense been battling back with us, too. So, vice versa. We've been having great days already. >> Is that communication different than what it's been in the other spots either here or Indie wherever you were? >> Uh, absolutely. I mean, absolutely. Yeah, I feel like not necessarily just the cuz I mean I've been around a lot of coaches that kind of coach the same thing, being loud in the m the meeting rooms and stuff like that, but it's just the the confidence of what guys are saying and knowing what their job is, knowing you know who their jobs relating to and stuff like that. So I'll say that's really the big difference of it. Not only just communicating and knowing your job, but knowing who you're talking to and you know who is that effect in the play or the scheme or however it goes. So feel like that's more the difference to where we're at right now. >> You talk about physicality of camp. Uh you like obviously you like hitting hitting guys. Yeah. >> You like where you are? You like to see more hitting? You like You think what you're doing now? >> Uh uh I'm honestly I mean I wouldn't say please. I mean it's good right now. It's good right now. We got a lot of young guys. Like I I keep saying it and I I'm going to keep saying it, man. The young guys right now, man, they're showing up on film. Uh specifically, I feel like in the safety room, you know, I feel like, you know, AC, Elijah Clark, uh Julius Wood, we got Ready Stewart back there playing a lot of safety reps and man, they're just showing up on tape time and time again. And not only just the physicality, but like I said, the the confidence that they're having in the communication and just the way they work, man. AC, I tell them all the time, man, feels it must be good to be young to be able to run all day cuz even after practice, you'll see him coming out here and not only will he work his technique, but he'll come out and he'll run routes for guys so they can get a look at certain stuff. So special type of player and I can't wait to see what his future holds for him for sure. >> How how good does it feel to see not see the coverage bust we saw last year? See guys making plays on the ball in practice, which we're seeing a lot. >> It's like a breath, man. It's like a breather, man. You know, especially for [screaming] a older guy like me being on the back end and considered the leader of the defense or the secondary and just a communicator, man. It it it's like it drives me crazy when when plays are given up like that. Now, if it's just a play that's just a good play off of a catch, you know, we play GP all all day every day and sometimes he's just a special player, you know, but it's just a complete bust and somebody's wide open like, yeah, it absolutely makes us, you know, upset, you know, we want to correct it right then and there, but at the same time, you got to have the next play mentality. But like I said, there hasn't been too many of those right now, you know, gracefully, but we want to keep it that way. We want to keep learning mistakes day in and day out. That's it. >> I'm sorry. Why is the Rams practice important for you? >> Uh, obviously, you know, the Ram, they they motion a lot. You know, there's not too many teams that we see, at least in our division, that motion as much as us as much as them. Uh, they got some great players up there. Obviously, Matt Stafford, you know, he's a great guy, you know, great quarterback, man. Been doing this for a long time. I feel like he's definitely top five in the league at what he does. So, being able to compete against, you know, one of the better uh quarterbacks in the league, and then just their their uh SC skill guys, too, on offense. They got Puka, got a couple other guys that are capable of making big plays. So, it's definitely going to be a challenge for us, but I feel like, you know, way we coming out here and stacking the days up against our offense who's I feel like the best in the league at what they do, man. It's I don't feel like there's nobody that we can't match up against. >> You remember going against them last year? What it was like out here? It seemed like they they got you guys a little >> Yeah. Yeah, it was like the same thing. I feel like last year we all lot a lot of uh big plays given up off of communication errors. Uh not only that, I felt like, you know, our physicality didn't really show us much that day. So looking forward to, you know, Tuesday and coming out here and being able to have a good healthy practice with those guys and obviously, you know, put our skills to test. >> Would you say that scrimmage and the first preseason game, even though you you have a lot of backups out there, that's really the test >> for this for the secondary and those kinds of things. >> Yeah. Yeah, absolutely. Like I said, we got a lot of young guys that we feel like capable of going there and playing. And, you know, obviously it's different when you got the older guys out there kind of, you know, coach you up as well as the coaches doing the same thing. So, we're all looking forward to kind of just seeing how they go out there and compete. Not only just compete, but how they, you know, face adversity because, you know, you know, preseason where a lot of young guys, they're playing not only just offense and defense, but the special phases of the game, too. And, you know, your legs get very tired. So looking forward to just seeing how they, you know, go against that adversity in the preseason when they're tired and being able to just still have the communication of where the standard is. >> You guys have three rookies that could play significant minutes for the season opener, the top three picks. Shotty said that you guys that they've earned it though. How have you seen those those three top three picks kind of go into the defense and earn that kind of play? >> Man, honestly, from you know, you hear all the stories about guys I mean Kayla's from, you know, alma moater and everything. So, I kind of already expected it based off of how they kind of prepped you coming into the league, uh, from Ohio State. Uh, but they kind of just came in and bought in, man. They didn't come in, you know, their head, you know, asking a bunch of questions as far as not just football related, but off the- field stuff. Came asking a bunch of questions. They came in competing and, man, they're just some dogs. They're just some dogs. They don't care who they're lining up against. You seen Caleb day in and day out lining up against CD and he gives him his respect. Obviously, it ain't nothing like that, but you know, he every play he gets a chance to line up against him, he feels like he's going to win that rep. And that's the type of mentality we want on this defense, especially coming from a guy that we're expecting to play a lot and not only play a lot, but to be a difference maker in our defense, man. Can't wait to see what he brings to the table this year, too. Cuz right now, man, he's everything they they they hyped him up to be, man. He's a special player. So happy to be here with him. Can't wait to see not only what this year brings for him, but, you know, the rest of his career cuz I feel like, you know, he keeps doing what he does and being the guy that he is. cuz like I said, he's a great football player, too. But he's also great guy off the field, too, man. He's humble, you know? He he he asks a lot of questions, uh, the right questions at that. And just the the, like I said, the humbleness that he brings, man. He he really doesn't talk much. He's not shy, but he doesn't say much. So, that's cool to be around another guy that not only was considered a high draft pick, but a guy that came from the alma mater to see how, you know, correlates from when I was in school to now. So, >> yeah. I know Chris Carter had a story about how the first time he met Caleb DS and Caleb said like, "Yeah, you know, I'm going to be the best one to wear with his number." >> Uh, did you hear other stories from Ohio State or people hit you up, like, "Hey man, you got Caleb. Let me tell you about him." Or anything like that. >> No, no, not really. I mean, once obviously we drafted him and everything like I, you know, I keep eye from a distance, you know, >> uh, just watching him throughout college. I thought he was always special. I seen a couple highlights when he was in Bama. never followed Bama or nothing like that, but as a DB, when you see another special DB and just that type of talent, you notice it and you kind of keep it from afar. And then when you end up going to Ohio State and playing and, you know, watching the game, seeing the type of player he was, being able to bounce from the different positions and him still make a difference in the game. But not only that, just the leading with conviction when he was out there, you know, at Old State. He does it out here, too, man. Like I said, he don't seem like a rookie at all. gets out there sometimes and there's sometimes, you know, as older guys, you know, you trying to figure something out or seeing too much and he's one of those guys that he'll echo the call just so you know that you're on the same page as him and stuff like that. So, like I said, he doesn't seem like a rookie at all. >> Do you think the the pace out here really prepares you for the grind? I mean, you're you're a defensive guy. You you like hitting folks is nice and cool, just good, bad. >> No, I mean, I think I mean, obviously it's different for each each player and stuff like that. you know, some young guys, you know, you feel like they need that cuz, you know, obviously the transition from collegiate level to NFL level as far as hitting. I mean, it's not that much of a difference, but it's a difference. So, you do want to get that, but also like like Fred Warner said the other day, man, tackling, it's like riding a bike at this point in my career. So, you just want to get out here and kind of get your body more so used to the physicality of it, not necessarily the the actual physical part of tackling. You want to get your shoulders, your neck, and stuff like that ready cuz take a year off or a couple months off from not hitting and going right back into hitting, your neck gets pretty stiff. So, that's more of the part of it. But, like I said, I I feel like we got young guys that have been professional this off seasonason. A lot of those guys, not only did we see them work uh they've been working kind of with a lot of guys throughout the facility and throughout the area where we was at. So, I don't think it's really going to be an issue with those guys, man. I'm just ready to see them guys go out there and compete. >> I got one more for you. Yes, sir. >> Talk a little bit about her appreciation day. what it means to to interact with the fans and have the fly over. >> Man, it's special. It's special. You know, obviously they've done a lot to uh serve the country, uh give us the freedom that we need, and you know, just the the the the respect of what they do for their jobs. You know what I'm saying? They respect us a lot for what we do, but you know, all in all, they're the real heroes. So, any chance we get to honor them and give back to those guys, you know, that's that's small thing for us. So, we try to do that as much as we can, sign everything we can. Obviously, we're on time crunch, you know, from time to time, but we try to do as much as we can just to show those guys on our way their appreciation for what they do. >> Appreciate. Thank you, sir. >> Yes, sir. Appreciate you guys.

title: Dak Prescott: "That's Who I Want to Win For" | Press Conference
text: def so much on the focus. Talk about how hard they've made it for you. Is there anything that stood out or a player that stood out about this defense so far through camp? >> Just their intensity. Um, you know, it' be I I don't know if I can just say one player because of the intensity. Um, you know, I think it might be the guy on the right. Then then, you know, that mean then the backers just as crazy or excited backing him up or, you know, then they're making plays for the DBs and so the DBs are, you know, screaming cuz they feel like they locked us down and, you know, it's like, oh, it's only the rush. But in times, you know, the rush gets there and the DBs do get a chance to make a play. Um, yeah, it's just the collab effort of their intensity and their communication is felt. It's definitely felt. Uh, when we're just out there and we're motioning and we're making our calls and then post play, anytime that they've made a play, they've celebrated deservingly so. And I just think that raises the energy of the whole team. Pisses us off a little bit on offense, but that's what camp's about. And, you know, we've just got to lock in and be sharper and fire back at him as we did today a little bit. Jack Todd Ar he's been. How did Flo ear earn your trust? >> Yeah, I mean speaking of showing up uh Flo is probably a guy the number one guy and and showing up uh this off season literally anytime I've had a ball he's been there. Um always asking questions, always just doing the right thing. Um he's the the he's a guy that you want on your team. He's a guy that you want on your team no matter what game you're playing. um his belief in himself. I think that's where it starts. And you know, the moment he's gotten his opportunity, he's never looked back. And not only never looked back, he's looking to to get more opportunities, to get more responsibility, to do more for the team. He understand the role that he plays. And um he's just trying to make sure that he capitalizes on it every time. And he's never satisfied. Uh he's a guy that I enjoy being around. Um he's a guy that I'm super thankful to to have as a teammate. And when you have that as a guy that's a pass catcher, it makes everything better. >> The leadership council um to have the 10 to 11 guys, whatever who it is, what's the benefit of that from the players perspective? >> Yeah, just that our voices are heard. Um you know, when you've got guys like we do on that council, veteran guys, you know, for me it's good to have guys on different teams. you know, I know what I know and good sometimes is a good thing, sometimes it's a bad thing, you know, and so you've got other guys that can come in and say, you know, this is a way that we've done it or I've had it like this in the past and you know, not necessarily those are the right ways, but it gives you a different perspective, gives you a way to look at different solutions to get to things. And um, you know, it's it's really cool how Shade put it together, you know, put it together with the O2X crew and just on the simple fact of, you know, there's certain things that we handle as a team. Um there's certain things that you know we may get and bring to a coach but not necessarily shotty you know and then we figure out a way to handle it and then there's things that ultimately have to get to the head coach and um I think that just takes pressure off of everyone's plate. I mean I know this council was created a little bit and in that sense you know I was made not to be the head guy like that was purposeful as you know I couldn't be the whatever you want to call it the chief leader in there because I'm going to speak up. I'm going to talk. I know what I know and I'm not going to be hesitant to say it, but we need other guys to take to take that lead. And you know, Kenny Clark, um Rashan, Gary, and Tyler Smith have have been those guys to step up and they're doing a hell hell of a job with the committee. And um yeah, there's things that from the spring to now that we've already incorporated that was the voice of that committee and that committee is ultimately speaking for the team. So, um it just allows it allows empowerment and um understanding that we we have a huge part in this uh this accountability thing. Tom Mashoto with the athletic uh Christian Parker talked to us yesterday a little bit about in the meeting rooms. He's got the guys making calls as if they were out on the field. It's got kind of loud in there a little bit. I was wondering if there's anything behind the scenes that you have noticed from the defense that maybe you're like, "All right, you know, I feel good about this. This isn't going to be a repeat of the way they were last year." >> Yeah, I mean, the men that we have and the way that they approach and attack their job. I mean, I can't talk about CP enough and the pride that he carries with his job. Um, you know, I was just talking to the couple of the trainers in there about, you know, the trash talk back and forth and I go, "Yeah, he can't be out there making the plays, but there's not one ounce of him that doesn't think that he's making plays." And he is. And that's, you know, having pride in your job. And I think that just ultimately rolls rolls into and it's contagious contagious to each and every one of those guys he's coaching. And I think that's where when I'm I'm speaking on the intensity. I mean, it starts with their communication and then ultimately ends with just how physical they are and running to the ball. And um yeah, there was a day the other day, you know, we're in the offensive meeting, they're in the defensive meeting and not that we were struggling to to hear what we were saying, but they were over there communicating and I don't know, I think it was a Jeopardy game within their own defensive calls and um yeah, it felt like playing on the road as we were just trying to install our meeting because of how loud and intense and fun that they were having doing their job. And um that's contagious as well. You feel that on that side of the ball, that unit's giving you that, you want to do the same on offense. So, um, nothing but good things to say about that unit. >> You've been coming out here now 11 years. Is there a part of this camp where, I don't know, week two, week three, when you're kind of like, I'm ready to go home. And if there is, is that any different than maybe when you were uh first on on the team? >> No, I love it out here in Cali. Um, you know, I was watching that fly over today, thinking about the weather, just thinking, damn, it's nice. Uh, [sighs] yeah. No, I love this game. Um, you know, fortunately my girls are out here. They're out here this week and so that that helps, you know, that helps even that time of my mind wanting to, you know, get away from camp and and um thinking about them, you know, they're down the road and so that allows me to get time with them. Um, but no, I've always enjoyed coming to training camp. There's never been even a moment of me that wants to get out, even when it's been a month and a half, whether it's three weeks or, you know, however long the the entirety of this thing is. I think this is the most that we get, especially in our organization of just pure football. uh you know and that's kind of why you know talking about all the goals and talking about all that you know is important to make sure everybody understands that that now cuz sometimes you get out here you're kind of in your bubble you know and you're just football football and then you get back to Dallas and then you know you start the normal the real life you know dealing with the things off the field whether it be with your family dealing with you know with the things that the media are going to say and then you know you're only in in at work talking about a game plan and it's very just a strict schedule where out here you've got time to create that brotherhood you know go and have sit down and have lunch with your guys and you know maybe take them out to dinner you know the nights that you can and so um I've always enjoyed training camp I think it's a huge part of a team success and I appreciate the way each and every one of these guys are approaching this camp >> Nick Harris forward start telegram shy complimented Tyler G for his start to camp what have you seen from your perspective >> yeah a guy that um that has a lot to prove um a guy that's walking around with a chip on his shoulder um you see it out there uh you know may may get beat play, but he's going to come back with more fire fire on the next play. And that's all you can really ask for a guy uh is to get better. He was an offseason award-winning champion. I think that speaks a lot about his approach to the offseason and and the gains and where he's trying to get to and what he's trying to to be for this team, understanding how vital that position is at left tackle. Um, you know, I'm sure he's trying to quiet the noise of Tyler Smith having to move or whatever the question was that you guys asked me the other day. Um, I'm sure he hears that and I'm sure he wants to, you know, make sure he solidifies not only his job, but who he is and the kind of player that he can be for this team and in this league. >> The Rams practice on Tuesday. More on that. They added a couple players on their side of the ball uh on on the defensive side. Do you see this as a litmus test for this offense right now? >> Yeah, absolutely. I mean, every day at practice is a is is a test and it's a it's a way to grade yourself. And then so when you ultimately get another team coming in here, um, and a team like the Rams playoff team, a really, really good team on all facets of the game, um, as you just said, adding some a big name, uh, a couple of big names, right? Whether it be McDuffy in the draft and whether it be Miles Garrett the other day and obviously they're playing with this Aaron Donald thing, so uh, thankfully he won't be out here just yet. Um, but seriously, yeah, it's a litmus test. Um, you know, it's it's all it's all you can ask for. CD was just talking about today. Looking forward to Tuesday and um it's looking forward to just us getting better, understanding one, this is a team that we're going to play in the season and it's probably a team that, you know, if we want to get to where we want to get to, we're going to have to see them again. So, um, called this probably what the first of three meetings I I'd assume if you know, everybody takes care of business and, you know, um, yeah, so it's definitely going to be a test. is going to be fun. It's going to be two great teams competing against each other and at the end of the day it's practice. So, uh, yeah, we'll have a lot of time after that to clean it up and to say this is what we got to get better, but we can't go out here and also have a hell of a practice and think we've done something. >> Tommy Arish, Dallas Cowboys.com. Going back to the leadership council, all four of the defensive guys weren't here last year. From your perspective when you've been around them, how have you seen them kind of grow into those roles in such a short time? >> I think that's who they are. Uh, honestly, I mean, I don't know if I I don't know them in their past teams, but I know the the men that I've talked to, I know the conversations that I've had. I know when I've sat in any meeting with them, whether it be these leadership meetings or team meetings, the way that they speak, the way that they articulate the game, their passion, their love for the game, uh, I think that's who they are. And so, um, it's really really cool just to to to, as I said, to be in a group like that and to have different perspectives and more importantly have people that are as hungry as I am and as urgent as I am to get this done. And so, um, credit to all all of those guys. Uh, they're they're real pros and they make me better and their their love and passion for the game and their passion for their brotherhood and their teammates, um, is felt. >> And then Cavonte Turban's a guy who got involved a bit today. How much more do you think he can do for this offense as a receiver? >> Yeah, I mean, a lot. I mean, Turb's a guy that we all understand he gets the ball in his hand whether it's the kick return, punt return, or jet sweep, or just in the in the passing game or whatever it is. uh you've got to watch out. And so um yeah, he's going to be a huge factor to this offense as he's been. And we're going to continue to try to find ways to uh make him compliment this offense, get us all better, complement those two those other, you know, two receivers out there. And um yeah, and he's a guy that takes pride in that, that wants to do whatever he can to to to help this team out. I mean, he knows a lot of my calls. He's a lot smarter um a lot smarter receiver than you probably may would think. And I mean, he's out there knowing all the adjustments, the hot adjustments. Um, he's he's just an impressive player. And so, if you ask even to go in there and block, he's going to do it. You know, he's been one of those guys that may get upset when you move him out of position because, you know, he's not the guy that you want to block. And, you know, he takes that offensive, you know, and that's just kind of the kind of guys you want. And so, um, yeah, we got to continue to find a way to get the ball to Tur, but once again, there's only one ball out there. And we've got a lot of great players. So, um, they've also got to do a job and compliment and make sure that they're doing their job to get others open. >> Scrugs, NBC5. Can you tell me your impressions of Kobe Durant so far in this game? >> Yeah, I mean, um, smart player, super smart player. I've had a few conversations with him just about the defense. Obviously, intercepted me the other day in the red zone and just going and asking about that defense and that call and the way that he played it, uh, that was impressive itself. Um and so um he's out there, he's fighting with two great receivers, three whoever whoever the hell is in front of him, he's he's fighting them and he's a guy that walks around with his chip on his shoulder, you know, talking about urgent and being a pro and doing the things the right way. Uh Kobe's one of those guys, you know, we're we also have this leadership group, but we also have these teams that, you know, we're all broken down into I don't know how many full teams it is, but Kobe's in my team. and um to hear him talk, to hear the way that he sees the game. Uh to to hear what this game means to him and how he would never cheat this game um is is is as great as a as a thing I've heard any teammate say. And so um he he's a he's a guy that not only speaks the right way, but walks it and you don't even have to talk to him and you can see what he's about and you can see what he means and how he's going to show up for not only this game, but for his teammates. a former Cowboy receiver recently talked about how he made $80 million and doesn't have most of it now. As a quarterback and the contracts you had, how do you make sure that you protect this wealth and things that you've gotten into your post career? >> Yeah, I mean I've got an amazing team, financial team. title: Ferran Torres Visits Ravens Training Camp | Baltimore Ravens Final Drive
text: When NFL players win the Super Bowl, they go to Disney World. When soccer players win the World Cup, apparently they go to Owings Mills, Maryland. That was the scene at Ravens training camp today as Spain's hero Feron Torres made a special appearance at practice. And for one day, the most famous footballer in Maryland wasn't wearing a purple jersey. Torres is in the United States on a press tour and he made a pretty memorable stop at the Ravens training camp today speaking to the team during the final huddle taking photos and spending time with players and coaches and he even left with some new Ravens gear. Torres exchanged cleats with Zay Flowers who is fresh off signing his new contract extension with Baltimore and he also swapped jerseys with Ronnie Stanley. Head coach Jesse Mentor pointed to Torres's World Cup performance as a perfect example of what it means to be ready when your number is called. >> We had a uh very special guest today, Fon Torres of Spain, game-winning goal in the World Cup. And uh it just kind of like really cool message. This guy came off the bench in the finals of the World Cup um in extra time, scored the game-winning goal. talk about just being ready when your number's called, being at your best when your best is needed. Uh, I mean, that's like the ultimate. So, it was uh such an honor and a pleasure to have him. >> That's a message that certainly fits a football team getting ready for a new season. You may not know exactly when your opportunity is coming. You may not know exactly what your role will look like, but when your number is called, you better be ready. And who better to deliver that message than a World Cup champion who knows exactly what that moment feels like. >> I think that says a lot uh for him, you know, being ready when your number's called. Um I think that can say a lot for, you know, a lot of people in this world, you know, just, you know, staying prepared, you know, cuz you just never know when your number's called. So, um even for myself, I never know when my number is going to be called. So, I got to stay ready at all times. For one day, Fon Torres traded the pitch for the practice field, got a taste of Ravens football, and left with a couple of pieces of purple to remember the day by. Not a bad way to spend a Thursday in Owens Mills. That's it for me today. We'll see you again tomorrow.

Uh because always things come up, even in the course of a 17 game season, you don't hit every situation and you don't end up in all those situations necessarily. So when you can do them and they're authentic, it makes people think, oh, you know, we could have done that here. We could do this here. Make sure we're good at that. Is everybody on the same page here? And I think Dan does such a great job of that throughout camp so that we're ready come week one. Do you feel like there's value of having starters in the preseason maybe from a procedural standpoint to for >> I think it goes both ways. I think there's so many factors that go into whether that happens and you know ultimately well above my pay grade so not worried about it. Hey guys.

title: Ahmed Hassanein's Feel-Good Story of Lions Camp
text: This is This is perfect. We'll get into the good news. So, give give me some early risers for you guys during training camp. >> I got a list, Will, so I'll let you go first and I'll bounce back off of that. >> Okay. Well, yeah. I mean, I I wrote some names down here, too. I I will start with I think the player that everyone is rooting for, and that's Ahmed Hassan. And look, he is the o most open of all books. And so when you get a chance to talk to Amed Hassan, you get not only his life story, but also a lot of really valuable insight into sort of how he is approaching the game this year versus last year and how he sees himself fitting in. And obviously he's made noise in the early stages of camp and and certainly with the two two PA practices, I think he's popped in both of those. And when I say he's making noise, literally he he he has a new routine of after making a positive play, flexing and roaring as loud as he can and oftentimes staring down the player that he just beat in a one-on-one rep as he did a couple days ago in a special teams drill against tight end Thomas Gordon. And the way Thomas Gordon reacted so casually and unbothered made me realize that everyone is just used to Amed Hosin roaring after big plays. and um he has been in the back field a lot I think in team drills and and he's getting pretty consistent second team reps now he's he's had a knack for for tackles for loss for for getting at least to the quarterback and setting up sacks for others which he would tell you was just as valuable as a sack of his own and it's notable here that he he's playing a different position this year in the Lions defense and even more notably to me is the fact that he's playing the position that he played throughout his time at college at Boise State he was the big end there playing opposite what the Boise State defense called the stud end, which is more of the traditional rush end in the mold of say Hutch or Derek Moore or DJ Wanom and that's what he was doing for most of last season. The Lions started him out last year as the big end, moved him pretty quickly to rush end. And so Amed spent most of his first season once he got healthy honing a new position, a a new part of his game. And I he also spent a lot of time watching film and studying guys like Hutch and other traditional rush ends past and present around the NFL. And you know in some ways might have lost sight just a little bit of what he does best and who he is. and he said this year he's kind of back to to being himself and he feels like his body type for one and his play style is suited to playing that hand in the dirt, do the dirty work, big end role and and I think so far we're seeing some fruits from that labor and look we can maybe circle back to this name when we get to three slow starters but you know I don't think it's a stretch to say that Hassan is is at least closing the gap if not on the level of Levi if you want to talk about big ends, potential big ends on this roster. And I I know they also see some interior value in Levi, but to me like Lacy clearly Tyler Lacy, another fast starter is clearly going to play a big role in this defense as the big end, but Hosanine is making a case to to be the number two in that department. And uh you know, he was walking off the field a couple days ago. Well, actually most days he seems to be walking off the field with Brad Holmes or finding Brad Holmes. And their conversation on Monday was uh a pretty sincere one where Hosanin actually teared up telling Brad how much he appreciates Brad, taking a chance on him, believing in him. And he told us yesterday, I think he told Colton the same thing when those two spoke a couple days ago that the response from Brad was awesome. And I want to make sure I get this right. So I'm going to pull up um the quote itself and the story I wrote today. But um so like you know Ahmed sitting there with tears in his eyes and and and just like stressing his desire to Brad to prove the Lions right to prove Holmes right. And uh he said Brad's response was um Ahmed you're proving me right by doing what you're doing and the big end role is going to be good for you. I'm excited for you. You're a football player. And Hassan told him he loves him because he loves everyone and Brad said I love you too. So, I know it's a long-winded answer, but I do think Justin, you probably agree that um we're seeing Hassan begin to climb the death chart in a pretty meaningful way because he's probably playing a role where he was he's more suited to play. >> Well, I can say this because I love you. All your answers are long-winded answers, my friend. [laughter] >> Uh yeah, Hassan's been awesome. And I think more than than Levi, it's Payton Turner is gaining ground on, >> right? That that's a guy I I thought highly of through OTAAS. I go, "Okay, I get it. I see the body type. I see the vision." Same thing we said with Marcus Davenport. The concerns were the same as Marcus Davenport in terms of durability. Turner practices once, hurts his back, hasn't been back to practice since. And so that's opened the door for a guy like Hos. I look at Levi. Uh Levi's been working mostly as a three tech through OTAAS and even into training camp. He does do some of the big end stuff. It's like a almost like a reverse flex for him. But uh I mean that's that's an interesting conversation regardless because he's been doing a lot of third team stuff. So uh I will stick with the other big end though. Uh Tyler Lacy I think is maybe the biggest surprise of camp for me. Um kind of a an afterthought in a lot of ways. Um and I feel like I should explain what Big End is to people that maybe don't know what it is. Um, when the Lions are in a fiveman front, typically for rundowns, the big end lines up directly over the offensive tackle, it's called a five-te. And then typically has a a more of a rush linebacker, your Derrick Barnes, your Trevor Noski to their outside shoulder. And so with with a Hosanine or a Lacy who's 300 lb, you know, the size almost of a defensive tackle, um, you know, allows them to lean into their their power. Uh, you still want some explosion there, but you want violent hands, the ability to shed. Hosinine's probably weakest skill is his bend. And so when you were mentioned, I I'd completely forgotten that he was playing Hutchinson's position and he was talking about mirroring Hutchinson last year. Like it's it's a ridiculous concept. >> Not going to happen. >> That's that's not his strength, right? Like Oene is a power player, so it just makes perfect sense that that's where they're putting him. But, uh, Lacy has been taking the first team reps at that big end spot and he's basically in like a a rotation with DJ Wam. Wanom comes in on pass downs, a little bit wider, fourman fronts, smart player, instinctual player. You can understand why the Lions him, but Lacy has been a force in camp. He's uh, done a lot of good stuff in one-on- ones. He's done a lot of good stuff in in team drills. He blowing up run plays the other day. Pressured Goff on a throwaway. pressure Teddy Bridgewwater on that long completion everybody wrote about the Dominic Love it that was actually a Tyler Lacy sack. >> 100%. I'm glad you said that. [laughter] >> Yeah. And so like it's a guy that I probably didn't think a whole lot about, but it's it's weird with those guys that get claimed off waiverss right before the season opener because they just get dropped in and expect to acclimate right away and it's so difficult. Tyler Lacy like Thomas Harper has gotten this full off season with the team and really kind of got to tap into what they know about him now, what he knows about the scheme now. And uh I mean like if I created a 53man roster like right now Tyler Lacy is safe, like exceedingly safe. I don't want to say lock, but like very close to a lock. Um and so that's that's been a really interesting one. >> Agreed. Jeff, anyone popping in the the Twitter sphere as as far as fast starters, guys who are making an an early push for a starting job or even a job on the 53 that that people are talking about out there. >> I think the big one and it's more of a personal one for me because um my co-host Boer went to SPSU, Nick Whiteside, who also went to school with my co-host Boer and he's well aware and I Boer used to tell me all the time about him and be like, "This guy's a grinder." you know, like when he first was on the practice squad >> back at SPSU, this guy used to be in the gym late. You know, he used to have a key to the gym working out. Now I see him making plays. I know we're going to talk about the cornerback two battle specifically.

title: Jordan Love: 'It's always our first chance to be back at Lambeau, being there with fans'
text: Family night as a father, what is that going to be like walking out with your baby? Or are you walking out with your baby? What's that going to be? >> Yeah, that's the plan. I'm excited, you know, first family night with the kid now. So, be able to be out there with all the other guys and and their kids. So, it'll be fun. I'm excited about it. >> Do you look at it differently now, approach it a little differently now? >> Uh no, I mean it's I think it'll be very cool. Obviously, it'll be something that, you know, we'll have a memory forever, something that we can look back on when he gets older. But, no, I really [snorts] don't approach it any differently. >> Football wise, is there anything specific you you want to get out of family night when you're at this stage of your career? >> Yeah, I think I mean football wise it's always kind of our first chance to be back in Lambeau, being there with fans. So, really that's our game environment. So, first chance to be out there, really just see how the operation goes, make sure everything's smooth. Then obviously it's always comes always comes down to the plays, make sure we're doing everything right, focusing on all the little details. But, I think just being in the environment kind of that game environment, our first chance to be out there in Lambeau, is always a test. >> What do you think of Marcedes' backflip? >> Man, impressive. Impressive. Yeah, I was like start to turn my back and then I I heard everybody going crazy and saw him doing the flip. But, it's impressive. I can't do that myself. >> Any favorite family night memory? >> I remember a couple of years ago you hit Samori Toure in 2022 for a touchdown. >> Uh favorite memory, I think the the favorite memory is doing the the net drill with the the quarterbacks and making them in the nets and hearing [snorts] the crowd go crazy. I always think that's the best part, especially like for young guys seeing it for the first time. Just kind of getting their reactions is always the best part. >> We saw Marcedes getting utilized a little bit in the passing game today. What can he add to this offense if you have him healthy for the whole season? >> I mean he just adds another playmaker. Obviously, very fast, very twitchy. And the things he can do and I think, you know, seeing more and more out of him in the passing game as well. Uh I think it's one of those things we're just going to keep building with him, keep keep improving on on things, but uh you know, I think he's going to be a great addition. It's just staying healthy um and get him out there, but uh just he adds another playmaker to our offense. >> All that said, any part of you that was like, "No, Marshawn, not a backflip. Like anyone else, just it's not you." >> Man, I every time somebody does a backflip, I'm I'm always thinking that. Like, "Oh, no." cuz I don't I don't know. It's dicey. I can't do it myself, so it's just it's scary, you know. You You don't want anything to go wrong, but if you can do it, you can do it. >> But but Florida did not >> Say it again. Sorry. Better than what? >> Cam Scarbrough's backflip. >> Did he do one? >> He did. He fell on it. >> He fell? Oh, yeah. See, that's exactly why it's it's hard. >> [snorts] >> He talked to him? Told him not to do it no more? >> [laughter] >> That's the last time we'll see any backflips again. >> He did a couple at your softball game, too, just before >> Marshawn? Yeah, he did. He did do some at the softball game, too, which, you know, I mean, hey. Maybe that'll be the last of the backflips we'll see. >> Jerry, how do you feel like the offense is progressing through the first week of camp? >> It's been good, you know, I think camp is just every day for us is is new installs, it's new plays. Um and I think you get to this point of camp where everything is in, and you know, it's trying to just build on the on the small details and the coaching points that we go back over when we get back to meetings. Um and just try to perfect our craft, but um yeah, it's obviously, you know, get get to this point for the young guys, it's obviously a lot with everything in. Um and I think for the older guys, it gets easier year after year, but it's always a challenge, you know, being able to go back once everything's in and kind of have the whole playbook in, and now we get to more of [snorts] the color period, it's how it is in the game, where it's kind of the whole playbook. So, um it's a lot to focus on as an offensive player, but I think we've done a great job, and and it's just about building on the little details, coaching points. It's never going to be perfect, uh but it's about, you know, finding the mistakes and correcting them. >> A weekend of camp, how different does it feel for you having your three primary guys that, you know, are kind of always around you as opposed to years past when it was a lot more free, obviously? >> Yeah, no, it's good. I think, uh for us, I think we've been getting a lot of good reps and, uh that's what you want. You want to be able to, you know, build a foundation in camp that's going to carry you out throughout the season. Um and I feel like we're getting on the same page with timing and, um just understanding where people need to be at in the offense and, um now it's just trying to find ways to do that every play versus different looks, um and trying to understand the offense as best we can, but it's always easier when you're out there with the guys that you're going to be doing it with during the season. Um having those guys healthy, being able to go, uh play after play, it's it's great work. >> Does it accelerate the timing at all when it's the same three guys for the most part? >> Yeah, I think it does, you know, I think, uh anytime you're with the same kind of crew, um and, you know, you can stay with those guys, you just you you build reps and you build trust and understanding of where guys are going to be and and where how things time up, um and then you can talk about stuff if, you know, the timing might be a little bit off, if um I was seeing something differently than they were seeing it, um that's when you can talk about it and you just continue to build and stack these things and that's what makes you good. >> Along those lines, what do you think you have with Saydou and Bow and Sky who were, you know, at some point those guys are going to have to play and their track records and their kind of limited track records of those three. >> Yeah, no, they'll play. Uh they'll definitely play a lot and, you know, I feel I feel like, uh you know, Bow's been here. Sky, obviously, is new to our offense, um but he's played a lot of ball. And then Saydou, you know, was here with us last year, so, um with those guys as well, it's just continuing to build. Obviously, they might be getting reps with Tyrod, too, um but, you know, we can learn from each other. Every time we're out there watching each other go, um we can still talk about certain things we saw, how we expect guys to run routes and just make sure we're still on the same page even though we might not be getting uh the reps together cuz you know that's how the season is. Things happen and guys will be out there. >> What's the comfort level with Jordan Morgan at left tackle? >> It's good. Jamo's got a you know a lot of ball [snorts] and reps under his belt. Obviously not all at left tackle, so you know I think he's been doing a great job so far and it's just continuing to stack, but you know once we get out in season I think we'll see more and more of what we might need to improve on and keep building on, but I think he's done a great job so far. He's been locked in and you know I think for him like I mentioned before it's good to be able to get you know kind of solidified in that one spot at left tackle. >> What are your early impressions of Sky? >> Man, Sky's been doing some great things. You know obviously I know Sky, I've seen him before playing-wise and he's another fast guy, but I think you know since he's got here he's definitely made some good plays and it's just you can see like his understanding of you know football and I think it was easy for him to kind of plug in and start making plays right away cuz he's just he's a smart football player and can figure things out, but I'm excited for him. I think obviously we haven't got as many reps together, but I think you know things once you get in the season he'll be out there for us. >> How much more comfortable is it this year with Sean at center given like there's been a bit of a crash course last year and then and then someone got hurt. You've got a whole off season with him now. Dan's thrown a lot at you. >> Mhm. >> And it looks like the communication at least between the two of you seems to be on point. >> Yeah, now the communication has been great. Um like you mentioned I mean last year you know things happen, injuries happen, you get thrown in that role where we hadn't had a lot of reps together and so we're trying to figure that out throughout the course of the season is definitely tough. So it's it's better to be able to get this OTAs, training camp and you know that's the communication is the most important part and like you said JG's been throwing a lot of different pressures at us which is great. It's great work for the O-line, the running backs, everybody, quarterbacks. Just be able to see stuff and make sure we're passing stuff off the right way. But Shawn's been good, man. He's been locked in and and I'm excited about him, but it's definitely nice for us to just be able to have this time to be working together versus how it was last year. >> Along the lines of the defense, how different of a look how does Zaire Franklin really make you think about it and challenge you as a linebacker compared to maybe what Clay Walker did last year? >> No, Zaire does a lot of great things. I mean, you talk about the looks, I think the whole defense right now is doing a really good job of just being tuned in with each other and and tied in to their disguise and making stuff look a certain way and then, you know, wait until the snap to be able to present whether it's, you know, pressure coming from left from the right, you know, whatever it might be. And so, it's it's definitely challenging as a offense as a whole for us with the O-line to be able to, you know, decide which way they might be coming with some of the pressures and you got safeties flying around all over the place, but Zaire, I mean, he just he's obviously the one running the show in the middle of the defense right there. And he does a lot of great things, you know. >> So, I'm excited to see him this year. Obviously, we've gone against him in the past, so I'm excited he's on our squad. >> He's part of the reason everybody's kind of tied together and on the same page on the defense at the moment. >> Definitely. I mean, when you're running the show as a defense, you know, you got to make sure everyone's tied in and and it's similar as offense, you know, it's kind of the quarterback of the defense and you know, I think X does a great job as well being in the post, but you know, I think it all comes back to them and JG how he's teaching it, but it's looking really good right now. I'm excited to see it, you know, when we get live. But, you know, they do a lot of great things and for a quarterback trying to undress it in the moment, it's definitely it's challenging. >> Jordan, how many times a day do you find yourself during practice looking over and seeing number 55? >> Oh, man, all the time. You know, Tuck's always around. He's always when we're doing team stuff, I feel like I always see him floating around somewhere. And whether he's doing his work or he's coming over and just talking or watching some of the reps to, you know, he's he's locked in. And I know he's hungry to get back out there and he's itching to get back out there. So, I'm excited to have him back. >> the biggest thing that he is going to really be impactful with once he comes back in the fall? Like, what's the biggest area where you're like, "Oh, this is going to >> You say it for him? Like, versus last year? For the offense as a whole? I mean, like I mentioned, you you need playmakers out there and that's what he brings to the table. Whether it's blocking, whether it's pass catching, or getting that YAC. So, he does it all. And obviously, the mentality he brings I think is another factor that gets guys going on offense and and guys want to be out there with him and and you know, giving their all. But, I think just it's kind of intangible, like everything he can do. Blocking, catching, getting yards after catch, and just bringing that mindset. >> Jordan, you've talked about becoming more and more of a vocal leader. I'm wondering how that pertains to talking to a young guy like Trey Smack. I know back in the day Aaron and Mason Crosby were really tight. Do you talk to him? Do you say he's he's got enough voices, I'm going to let him focus on what Cam Akers is saying to him? Or or how do you approach that? >> Uh I mean, we'll talk to his teammates, but as far as, you know, kicking and doing that stuff, I'll let him do his thing. You know, he he's a pro. That's what they brought him here for. And obviously, I don't know how to kick a football, so I'm I'm I'm going to leave that to him. But, as far as teammates, you know, I always do my best just to have relationships with guys, be able to talk to guys, encourage guys whenever, you know, they might need that. But, for him, you know, I know everybody in here has got a job to do. And I know he'll be he'll be great at doing his. >> You never kicked before in your past? >> Nah, man. That's That's not for me. Feet are too big. >> If they asked you to, could you step up? >> Could I step up and make a kick? I mean, yeah, if you asked me to, I I could try. [laughter] I don't know if I >> Like, where are you on the emergency kicker depth chart? >> pretty low. Pretty [laughter] low. We'd probably go for two before we're kicking. >> Uh Jordan, during the offseason program, McVay said that he was going to take a look at this offense and strip things down. As you're throwing these installs, from your point of view, is this offense different heading into training camp than it was maybe in years past? >> Yeah, I mean we talk about you know Matt kind of going through the offense and and we we did that. He did. He went through and you know, I think it's really more of how we install plays and kind of the grouping of the plays we install each day. He's went back through and changed some of the things to put more of the plays we run a lot more throughout the season towards the front and kind of in a group and some of the plays we might not run as much towards the back end and really taking out some of the plays that you know, we might be practicing a lot and those situations or that play really isn't good for us in the season. >> So did you guys sit down together and go through that? >> That'll be stuff Matt and you know, the staff will do kind of during the break before OTAs and you know, he'll hit me on some stuff and we'll talk about it. I think when we get back for OTAs, that's when we really talk about it in depth and and kind of go through it stuff together. >> Jordan, how often like during a season do you get into a game or a situation and Matt will call a play and you're like, we haven't run this since camp. Does that happen? And is that why you're running >> [clears throat] >> everything you can now? >> Yeah, I mean there there is situations where that might happen. Definitely. I mean you got you look at the installs we have. We have so many plays and you know, a play might get run one time during camp and it might come back up throughout the season. But I feel like for the most part a lot of that stuff is more kind of kind of the end of game situation stuff we have end of half end of game those two-minute plays where you're getting some of the unique defenses where it's like that fence line defense with everybody on the sideline. So some of those unique situations you're just not practicing as much. We might walk through it a lot during this time and then you get to the season and that's stuff that you might not practice as much and it's just everybody's got to be locked in because these moments come up and the play will get called and everybody's still got to be able to go out there and execute. >> Jordan, two more. >> Speaking of you kicking, that reminded me you were at the World Cup. What's up with you getting booed in LA, man? >> Oh yeah, I don't know. I don't know. It was pretty crazy. Um >> Was it the Rams fans? That's what I said. It must be a lot of Rams fans there. Um but, you know, huh? We'll take over that stadium when we go out there. Yeah, I think for me, it's really just finding there's going to be times where I might need to do stuff like that, where there's pressure, you know, there's guys in my face where I'm I have to drift to kind of be able to create a throw. Um and there's times when I'm in the pocket and I found myself doing things where that I'm off balance on my feet when I don't need to be. And so, I think it just comes back down to understanding, you know, when I have a clean pocket, when I have time to set my feet and be um as balanced as possible. I think that's when I'm at my best. So, um understanding that there's just there might be times where I need to do it, like you said, and there's times where I don't. So, it's anytime I can be balanced in the pocket, you know, throwing out breaks to the left, not falling off, like little things like that, um is what I just want to focus on right now. >> Jordan, how much do you talk to Jonathan Gannon about what he's doing in practice, and does that help you? >> Yeah, we talk a good amount, you know, after some of the team periods, uh you know, he'll talk to me about some of the disguises, ask me what I'm seeing, like how do how do I like some of the disguises. Um and we'll talk just about some of the coverages they're running, and um I'll ask him questions about what I'm seeing out there and and what he's trying to do, um or make the offense think. Um but, I mean, that's just how it is. You go back and forth, and, you know, it's good on good. We're trying to make each other better. Um obviously, all with the goal of uh going and playing everybody else throughout the season.

title: Brian Gutekunst: 'It's one of my family's favorite events'
text: Good. Getting ready for family night? >> [snorts] >> Good. >> You going? >> Huh? >> As of now. Actually, it's my it's my family. It's like my kids and stuff. That's one of their favorite events. I think they they love the fireworks. So, yeah. Ted used to get really mad cuz we were all on the field watching the fireworks every every year. He'd be like, "You didn't go down there, did you?" I'm like, "Well, yeah, I went down there." He's like, "Yeah." >> What else are you supposed to do? >> Right, yeah. You were He was the best would be like the Mike would Mike would call the team up and and he'd already be gone cuz he was going to, you know, he he wanted to beat the traffic. So, he He's like, "Yeah, cuz I watch the fireworks on TV last night." There's people on the field. Did you know that? >> [laughter] >> So, yeah. That was the best. So. Shoot. >> What have you seen from Cece the first week of training camp and how's it compared to the guy I don't know if there's anything that surprised you at from the guy that you saw during the pre-draft process on tape? >> Yeah. No, I mean, he looks like the guy, you know, that we that we we evaluated. I think I really like how he's competed. You know, he's shown up every day. He's been prepared. I think the, you know, the coaches are very happy with how he's been intentional about his preparation. Um, you know, even though these guys have come out of some pretty good programs in college, the NFL's different and uh, you know, every day is a bit of a challenge and uh, I think they like how he's approached it and uh, certainly that you guys have seen too. He's He's held up pretty well. Long way to go, but I think he's had a nice start to camp. >> As far as starting with family night, is is in the grand scheme of things is family night just a practice for you as far as evaluating that? >> It is It is, Bill, but I said that at the same time and I know I've talked about this before. I think the luxury we have is having 60-some thousand, 70,000 people in there and that always ramps up the urgency and the intensity for these guys. Um, so we're really lucky to have it um, for that that and I do think, you know, again, um, every practice matter matters, every rep matters, but there are some with the preseason games and joint practice and and family night. There's just some markers I think that maybe mean a little bit more, you know, just because it's uh, um, the urgency and competitiveness might be ramped up a little bit, but it is just another practice and it's like you know not good or bad, however guys fare in it, it's onto the next, you know. >> Do you feel like you've got an extra draft pick with John Williams? I mean, he's playing really well. I kind of was surprised. I got to admit I was not he was not top of mind coming into camp. >> Yeah, it's it's great to see him out there, you know, after a full year of him kind of you know being a rookie and then and not being able to compete, but you know, go to meetings every day and do all the things he was doing. I'm sure he's he's pretty eager to get out there. Yeah, I got to remind guys, you know, he's done for what he's done so far in a week has been pretty impressive with the fact he hasn't played football in a year, you know what I mean? So but no, yeah, it's really you know, it's really good to see him out there and again, he's he's been competitive. They've moved him all around. I think he's played almost all five spots, you know, which you know, is a is music to my ears, but uh at some point I think he'll start to start to settle in somewhere so we can get a really good look at him. I'm excited to see the preseason games and and see what he can do there. >> Coach, Frank Lomax 30 years old, that's getting up there, especially for that position. What traits did you see that made you want to go >> Yeah, I know and I talked about it before how much we kind of liked him coming out and then they certainly what he did early in his career. You know, but I think he's he's really decisive. You know, I think you guys have seen that too. His his instincts are are very good. He reacts very well. He's downhill player. He's very physical. He plays with an edge and then you know, just having him here for the time we've had him, his communication, his ability to kind of lead the defense the way Jonathan wants him to is been he you can mean you can tell he's done it a while. text: [music] >> Welcome into Jags AM. It's practice day seven. We're officially in week two of Jaguars training camp at this point. No fans in the house today, but [music] a lot of work going to get done and they're getting prepped for their mock game that's going to take place tomorrow. So we welcome you in to Jags AM brought [music] to you by Fields Auto Group. I'm Kainani Stevens. Brian Sexton and John Oehser are with me today. Let's get into our big things. We got a whole week to recap for you. They're brought to you by GEHA Government Employees Health Association. Big thing number one is the pads went on on Monday and Jacoby Myers talked a little bit about his philosophy for the offense when the pads go on. >> Well, I'm going to just tell the guys be aggressive first and then if you got to pull it back, it's easier to go backwards than to try to go out there, feel it out, get hit in your mouth and now you think you're about to go hit somebody. It's not going to work like that. So, be aggressive first and let them pull you back. >> So pads went on on Monday and I think day one fair to say the offense looked a little bit better than the defense. Normally it's the opposite, but uh that's a good philosophy to have. You never want to go in halfing it. You want to go full 100% and then pull back if you have to. >> 100%. You'd rather deliver the blow than have the blow delivered to you. And and the first place that I went and I was really gratified to see that Liam Cohen put the pass rush party down in front of the fans, right? You had the the offensive line against the defensive line and that's to me that's always the most fun part of training camp cuz we've talked all through the off season, John, about waiting till the pads come on to be able to evaluate the big guys. And of course we had a story immediately with Anton Harrison and how well he has transitioned from the right side to the left side. And listen, I I think that's permanent. They're not necessarily going to say that now, but it's contract year for Anton. He's motivated. He told me walking off the field after the first day in pads he liked it. He enjoys being back on the left side and it's a big move for the Jags. >> Yeah, I didn't have a chance to talk to Jacoby after he spoke, but it sounds like at some point he got knocked on his butt. >> How do you learn? Real quick. >> And uh so uh absolutely one of the sort of uh percolating stories of training camp is what you just talked about. Uh Antone Harrison, it it feels like uh they've been sort of having that move on the back burner for some period of time. With Jawaan Taylor out this time, it it sounds like they just kind of said, "Hey, see how you like it." See if it's okay. We'll see what's And now all of a sudden you're what? Four, five days into it. I'm with you. I I I can't guarantee that he's over there full time, but if he's your best, most talented tackle, if he likes it there, if it's starting to happen, you know, so much has happened since this regime has gotten here organically where it just feels right. All of a sudden the move with Antone Harrison to left somehow feels like it's happened organically and maybe that sticks. >> One other guy that stood out, Kai, and and I'm sure you saw him too and and it's a story because last year at this time he wasn't on the field. Eric Armstead, really in that first day of pass rush party he dominated and it was good to see cuz he's a 12-year guy and he's going to be important for them to get push in the pocket. So immediately with the pads coming on practice got a lot more interesting. >> Yeah, seeing him healthy is also key as well. Our second big thing is going to be bounce back. When we talk about day two of pads, that was certainly a dominant defensive day and coach Campanelli said he likes to be honest with his players more than gassing them up too much. >> I just believe in being honest and you know, even with anybody perceives as a great day, it isn't all sunshine and rainbows, you know, you got to tell the truth and uh you got to see around corners and see what the problems lying ahead are. You know, it might not get you here, but uh my college coach, Coach Iano, used to always say that all the time, "It don't get to you when it gets you." And um you got to be on that. And I think that's a huge part of of coaching. So, um, never as good as you think it is, never as bad as you think it is, but you got to be honest. It's the only way for anything to get better. It's the only way anything improves. >> It's a little bit of a dose of reality, John, from camp. And he keeps it real, of course. But, day two defense looked amazing. Jalen Jones was out there flying around. Eric Murray, the DBs. Not uncommon to see early on in training camp, but kind of good to see it go back and forth cuz that means, you know, you're not totally one-sided. >> Yeah. I laughed because I got a question from somebody um after the Was that uh Tuesday when the defense looked so good? Um, [music] are you worried about the offense? Well, I saw the offense for 10 games at the end of last season look like one of the best in the NFL. >> I think we'll be all right. >> I saw it for the first four or five days of practice look like one of the best in the NFL. And so, they had one bad day. So, uh that's the world we live in, Brian. >> You know, I didn't I've been talking to a lot of the ticketing folks that are uh the prospects who were here before the day begins, and I always challenge them, "Hey, where's the weak spot on the roster, right? You guys tell me where you see a spot that you're worried about." Um, and nobody really comes up with one. I mean, they they talk about the running back because Travis is not here, and the linebackers. But, the fact of the matter is that on any given day, you you're going to find a spot where you're like, "Whoa, you know, what was that?" And as you said, back and forth, Kai, we have seen a bad day for the quarterback turn into a good day the next day. We've seen things where the offensive line or the defensive line has rebounded, and that's what training camp is all about. It's about figuring out that rhythm and building the consistency. If you ever have a perfect practice, please let me know. 33 years of doing this, I've never seen one. >> Yeah, you also don't want uh it to be perfect offensively every day because this is practice. Meaning, you want to practice things that maybe you're not as good at. You want to throw situations at them that they're not ready for. If if he's going 25 for 25 every day, then you wonder are you are you are you testing things to see if they're going to work. So, uh Look, it it was not a great practice Tuesday. I don't know if you guys remember or not, last year's mock game was I mean >> a mess. >> It and it it it was panic at the gates after that. Oh, they're going to be awful. They're going to be This is a long process and one practice that's good for the defense. Uh that's okay. That's okay. >> And I I think it bears mentioning at least from my point of view. I didn't feel like Trevor was making mistakes or there was a lot of error. It was like some of the defensive plays were very impressive. So, I feel like you have to give credit where credit is due there. It's not always a mistake by somebody. Sometimes it's another person playing really well or Trevor delivering it to the perfect spot. You can't defend it. So, it's a little bit of both there. >> Somebody's got to win, Kay. You know what happens then? Somebody's got to lose. >> And one's got to lose. Our final big thing today is going to be the mock game. We mentioned it. Last year was very telling. They had some troubles getting going, penalties, issues. So, what they're going to do is basically have a scrimmage out here at practice and fans are invited. So, sign up and come out if you can tomorrow. And uh they set it up like a game and they really run it that way, timeouts, all that. And uh try to get the most out of it cuz obviously these guys have been in the building for quite some time working out OTAs, off-season program, but there is something to actually playing a game, dealing with it as it comes along and uh seeing how they deal with those situations. >> Yeah, and um I think not every fan follows it the way we do, Brian. Um not every team anymore does something like this. Uh sometimes you'll see on the schedule mock game and then you go out and it's it's barely recognizable. There's really no game format to it. Uh Liam does it much more old school in that sense. Uh again, part of it obviously they get a lot out of it. And he also likes to give the fans something from time to time when they're out here. So, it's another example of of this franchise trying to do things that way. >> And they also they prepare for everything, right? And you've got a lot of guys who are here who don't know how it works on the sidelines. They don't understand the process that the coach goes through on the sidelines. And he wants them to be up to speed so that next week in New Orleans it doesn't appear new to them. Um I The scenarios they go through, not just on the field, but on the sidelines are important for them to be a cohesive team. We both have seen times where the Jaguars in their history have not looked all that cohesive on the sidelines. >> never seen that. >> Yeah. This team is not going to have that problem. >> I do want to mention as well, you don't read entirely into what the lineups look like in these practices, but offensive line specifically, we've seen Anton moved to left tackle. Uh so, this could give us a little bit of a preview what they might be working out on offensive line and what they want to do there. >> Well, and and so, you're not going to have Cole Van Lanen at least in the preseason. If if Patrick McCary's back doesn't allow him to play, here's Wyatt Miller, right? We've seen Jawaan Taylor have a really strong camp with Robert Hansley as the established starter. He's pushing there. And Walker Little has worked at both guard spots at various times throughout camp, as well. >> Yeah, keep on getting emails better they're going to trade Walker Little, Walker Little this, Walker Little that. He can do a lot of different things. >> A lot of starts in this league. >> And he's working at a pretty reasonable number, about 15 million. >> Yeah, I don't think we're at a point where we're trading anybody right now.
