title: Colts' Daniel Jones continues to impress, 'Did everything tonight'
text: Here we are from Grand Park. The Colts just finished up their seventh practice of this training camp. Fireworks going on behind us. As you can see, it was an energized practice here uh for the Colts night practice of training camp. I'm Nathan Brown, your Colts insider with the Indianapolis Star. He's Joel A. Ericson. He's the one that watched practice tonight. I was driving back from Canton talking to Adam Venitary ahead of his uh Hall of Fame induction on Saturday. So Joel will give us a little bit of an insight on what took place here at Graham Park tonight. Joel, I know you were very enthused about what you saw from Daniel Jones in this extended practice tonight. We had a lot of team versus team action. What did Daniel do that impressed you so much? >> Well, I I think I think Shane Stiken really summed it up at the end of the practice. He was asked, "What more can Daniel do? What more do you need to see from Daniel?" And he said, "Well, he never got anywhere because we saw him do everything tonight. There were two scrambles where he had to step up, navigate a a pocket, and then take off. And he looked for the first time, I think, in this camp like Daniel Jones scrambling last season. He made some gorgeous throws. There was a a ball up the seam to Tyler Warren. He hit Ulissiz Bentley the fourth on a touchdown pass. There was another touchdown pass to Ashton Dulan. That was an absolute laser in the red zone. He was just very, very good. I don't have the numbers on me right now, but I think he was going to be like 75% completion and a lot of big plays. He's just very very good. And we're at the point now where like like Shane Syen was saying, I just don't know what more we need to see from him. Um I know we just talked to Shane after practice, some hamstring injuries starting to crop up on this team. Um a handful of guys, Hunter Wer, uh Laquan Treadwell, DJ Giddens. um any of these injuries that we're starting to hear about along al along with Alec Pierce who we still do not have a great timeline for. Any of those injuries starting to concern you at all? >> CJ Allen. CJ Allen I think is the one that's the biggest one just because of the role that he's expected to play. Hunter Waller is going to play a role on this defense, but it's not going to be the same as CJ Allen. CJ Allen is supposed to be the starting middle linebacker. He's supposed to take every snap. And the longer he's out, he was out for two days with a calf injury. They've been rotating. Now he's out with a hamstring. You don't know how long that's going to linger. It It does get to the point where you start worrying about how much time he has on task and whether or not they're going to have to mix and match and maybe not give him that middle linebacker role right away. This actually is why Louis Anarumo is experimenting with giving Cam Binham the green dot. >> Yeah. Um we'll see how Hunter Waller, DJ Giddens, guys that have missed a couple days of practice now, how that might affect their positional battles on the starting offense. Wer of course um battling for one of those safety positions with uh rookie AJ Hulsey. Um DJ Giddens for that start or that backup line or backup running back spot with uh Seth McGawan, a fellow rookie. So um we'll see when they might get uh chance to come back. Hamstrings a little bit. Um something that teams are a little bit cautious with, something that can um nag on for a little bit. So we'll see um when they come back. We now have a day off before a uh back-to-back set of practices on Saturday and Sunday. We'll be back here uh from Grand Park on Saturday. Uh before then, check indie.com. I've got a story running tomorrow from talking to Adam Venitary today in Canton. We'll have several stories from practice here today and get you ready for two more days of training camp here at Grand Park. For Indie Star, I'm Nathan Brown. He's Joel A. Ericson. Thanks for watching this edition of Indie Star at Grand Park. [laughter] >> So, how quickly did things progress or did it seem like things were already pretty close? >> Things were definitely progressing. Like I told you guys, I I always had faith and it just a matter of time. It takes times to work, take time to work through uh kind of those things, those deals. So, just being able to stay patient and just knowing that, you know, both sides wanted the same thing. We had a common goal. You feel like this is a commitment to show you. >> And like you said, it's a commitment. It's a commitment not only to myself and my family, but uh like I said, I've always said throughout the years I wanted to be here, you know, for the rest of my career. So, like I said, we all had the same common goal. >> Did Bean's deal getting done, did that help speed things up or um were you did you feel like things kind of happened independently? >> I I think it happened independent, but obviously, you know, sometimes those things do have influence. You know, it gives people ideas, things to work off of. So I I think to an extent it definitely played a part for sure. You know, obviously every deal does. You see someone uh just went today, you know, shout out to Jir as well. So >> is it is it meaningful to you to be part of this this core of running backs that seem to have kind of changed the trajectory of of how from a business standpoint of how these guys are treated? >> It does, but I mean it it it was progressive. I mean, if you look over the course of the years, it was progressive from, you know, you look at McCaffrey and Saquon and, you know, the different backs that it definitely was a thing that progressed over the years. So, that's why I always say it's a work in progress. Um, but it all starts with putting a good product on the field. >> Looking at your history from college until now, you had a lot of carries and things like that. Uh, you're going to keep saying it until something happens. So, it's my job to just continue to take care of my body and keep doing what I'm doing. >> You talk about commitment and this team giving you that. What is it about being part of this team that excites you and why you wanted to stay here? >> Well, number one, I think it's not only the players that we have from an onfield perspective, but the type of guys that they are from an off-field perspective. So when you have a team like that, the sky is the limit. >> Many running backs have signed three contracts with one team. Does that mean something to you? >> It does. I think you mentioned it earlier, the commitment that the the club has towards me, but also the commitment that I have towards the club of that I want to definitely be a part of helping this organization and this team win and win for a long time. >> Thanks, Jonathan. >> Great. So, special night for everybody. It was good back and forth. Uh, defense we kept score. They won tonight. Um, it was great. It came down to the wire there in a two-minute drive. He wasn't holding in, he wasn't holding out. For sure. >> Those two scrambles when he came up through the middle, it looked like he really >> maybe for the first time like got to full Daniel speed. >> Yeah, it looked good. It sure did. So, that was exciting to see. Very encouraging to see as well. So, I love where he's at. Um, it's awesome to see. Do >> you have your plan together yet for preseason next week? >> Uh, we're working through that. I'll probably have that later on this weekend. So, go for there. Are you looking for the other quarterbacks? Are you looking for a little more consistency there? And what what are you kind of working through? >> That's it. I mean, that's the guy that's going to be the most consistent that's going to win that job. And so, um, those guys are battling. It's back and forth right now. And obviously, we'll grade the tape, go through it, and, uh, get better every day. >> Have you seen consistency from them yet or [snorts] do you think >> I think there's been flashes? I think there's been flashes. Um, but yeah, there's got to be work to done for sure. >> What did you see from Nick West? Just his ability to continue that play down the field. >> Yeah, he's he's making a ton of plays. obviously had a good uh little bench route, a little seven cut uh today, but um he's a guy that's a veteran player that's made some plays in this league and so he's been consistent uh throughout it so far. So I'm excited about where he's at. >> CJ Allen today. >> Yeah, he's dealing with the hamstring right now. >> Is is Ulys's Bley kind of taking a step for you guys kind of forcing his way to the running back? >> Yeah, I mean tonight he made a ton of plays. Obviously had a little double move for a touchdown and then out in space made a couple guys miss. Um so that was great to see. You know, he's made great strides. you know, he did a hell of a job last year for us on the practice squad and uh obviously making plays out here in training camp. So, it's great to see >> that last situational down eight. What was the situation there? >> Well, we're just keeping total score throughout the whole thing. So, that was 46 seconds left. Balls on the 25 was a two-minute situation. No timeouts. If the offense scores, they get seven points. You go for two. Um and the defense gets a stop, they get seven there. So, it was down to the wire. Um it was awesome. >> What do you think about the DJ to do one back end? >> It was great. Um, I think those plays, we got to make those plays and, uh, it was just a hell of a throw. Tight window throw. He got both feet down. It was great to see. >> Shane, I know you talked about him the other day, but AJ getting some first team reps on defense. Just over the course of the last week, how have you just seen him grow? >> Um, he's grown tremendously. I think he's got a high football IQ, which is awesome, and you need that at that position and the safety. There's a lot of communication on the back end that goes on. Um, high football IQ guy, like I said, and uh, he's making plays and he's stepping up. and AJ's battle um in that safety spot with Hunter Waller. Do you have any sort of updated timeline when you would expect him back? >> I don't. He's got a hamstring. So, um hopefully sooner than later. >> Any update on this? >> Uh no, not right now. His rehab's going great. I'll say that. He's going great. I don't have the time table on his return, but he's doing a hell of a job in his rehab process. >> Shane, you talk about you talk about what you see from Daniel day after day. What What do you need to see next? Well, [laughter] well, um, I think, you know what, he's doing a tremendous job. I mean, the biggest thing, I mean, we want to keep him healthy. That's the biggest thing. We want to keep him healthy all season. Um, cuz we saw what he did last year, and I think we can recreate that, um, if he's healthy out there. I, you know, I got a lot of confidence in these players, a lot of faith in our guys to go make plays. So, um, I'm excited about that going forward. >> All right, last one here. Um, what is he dealing with right now? >> He has a hamstring as well. >> Yeah. >> All right, JT up. What have you come to appreciate about Jonathan Taylor over the last couple years? >> Everything. I mean, you know, just seeing him run down the field and uh getting all those yards. I mean, it's it's great watching him, great playing for him and uh you know, we have confidence up front blocking for him. So, it's it's been great. Yeah, we're excited to have him back. >> Matt, working with Daniel, seeing him back in action, what does that do for this team from just a inspiration standpoint? >> Oh, it's great. I mean, you know, it's it's uh it's exciting to have him back. I mean, it's a good refresher to see him back there calling the plays. you know, it's a familiar voice and uh you know, gets us fired up. We're ready to go. We're ready to block for him and gives us a little bit more motivation and uh you know, we really appreciate how much he effort he's put in to get back here and uh yeah, I'm excited to have him back. >> What's the atmosphere like? What's the atmosphere like when a player gets rewarded like Jonathan did today? What's what's it like just when you when you see him for the first time out there? >> It's exciting. title: Gritty, gator-hunting guard Wyatt Teller: Texans will be 'special'
text: Hey guys, Aaron Wilson. Happy to bring you an exclusive interview with Texans left guard, former Pro Bowl selection Wyatt Teller. A legend in many ways. gritty, tough, hard-nosed, nasty offensive lineman, shifting to the left guard position after playing right guard for the Cleveland Browns for a very long time, playing at a very high level, and now after playing his trade for the Cleveland Browns, joining the Texans, injecting toughness, leadership, and tenacity. He's got a real book of business. I call it built on knocking people down, stonewalling pass rushers, blocking downfield, opened a lot of pathways for Cleveland Browns touchdown runs, especially during the good years of Nick Chub. I think he'll do a lot for this team on and off the field, blocking for CJ Strad, who recruited him to the Texans, had a hand in this addition to your $23 million maximum value contract. And also they share a bond. They met at a Christian seminar and are two faith-based guys. And I know that Wyatt and his family, Carly Whiting Teller, they've really taken to Houston. He loves the barbecue. He loves the community, loves the real sense of camaraderie that he has in this locker room. Feels like this is a special place. He's very excited and wants to get back to the kind of football that he had played in the past. And you know, one thing he's very adamant about is not trashing the offensive lines the past. I know that people have been displeased with the group in the past, but you know, as he said, hey, they were in the playoffs. You don't do that with a bad offensive line. He's right in the sense that they only allowed CJ Stra to be sacked 23 times last season. Run blocking wasn't great, but neither was, you know, not having a Joe Mixon that that really affected things. So, it's a lot of things can be true. He's lined up next Arie to Ursery and Keelin Rutled along with Jake Andrews as they continue to compete for the center job. He's very excited about what he's seeing from Rutledge who is one tough customer, Big Red. So these guys are like two peas in a pod, two legitimate tough guys along with Ed Ingram. The interior, they've really injected toughness and physicality. So we'll bring you this conversation. As um I said, you know, they made an investment in him. 5.75 million signing bonus. Eight and a half million total guaranteed annual 500,000 per game active roster bonus incentives negotiated by Andy Ross who also did business with the Texans on the Javian Clowney one year up to $8 million max value. But this guy all pro bowl with the Browns and of course met Strad at Proathlete Outreach Seminar about a year ago in Dana Point, California. And then they ran into Stra this year at the same conference, East Coast. And so he was recruiting him, recruiting the wife, Carly Whiting, and just talking a lot about, you know, the situation. But you'll hear some stories from Wyatt in a moment about the alligator hunting that he did in Florida and relearning playing left guard because he, you know, punched with his right hand for so long. And so that's an adjustment. But last year he you know missed a you know actually last two seasons combined missed a combined eight games but he allowed just three sacks and 9.8% quarterback pressure rate. Wants to get back to his old allp proing form. I feel like they went through some tough times some growing pains. They went away from the running game but he is here to run the ball with grit and toughness and protect CJ Stout. So likes what Cole Papovich is all about. very excited to be a part of the culture and you know everything that they're doing here and wanting to win a championship. So, you're going to hear from Wyatt in his entirety with everything from the fan base to playing a new position, the mentality here about what he thinks of the offensive line, and of course, uh, his relationship with CJ Strad, being from, you know, the Northeast, playing at Virginia Tech, growing up from the Northern Virginia area, DC area guy like myself from in the city, right in DC, but, you know, he's from Northern Virginia, not far away. So, we had a good conversation about that and his adjustment to Houston, Texas, such a big city, biggest city he's ever lived in. Loving the culture, loving the barbecue. Uh, sometimes he misses the mountains of Virginia, but really liking this part of Texas. And so, you hear from him about Rutled blocking for David McGomery, Woody Marks, and so much more, including that famous alligator story. I don't want to steal too much of the thunder. I do set it up for you. He went viral in 2021 because he hoisted this massive 200lb 10- foot alligator over his shoulders and carried it with his bare hands. He was visiting Florida, NFL offices, went on a gator hunt with Miami Dolphins defensive tackle Zack Syler. So this was at a legal year round free range gator hunting ranch. And they legally hunted and put him down and then he wanted to transport the heavy reptile by himself throwing across shoulders like a sack of feed. And that gave social media really a jolt. Uh just showed more rugged old school. People called him a human snowplow in the field. Uh you know, some animal rights activists not thrilled, but totally legal within his rights. He's an outdoorsy guy, a hunter, and he took down a apex predator, turned him into a trophy. That said, uh he has a lot of respect for wildlife and does things the right way within the rules of what it takes to be a hunter. So just keep that in mind. but absolutely a real dog on the field, a tough guy and someone that is very respected in the NFL community around the league. So, when they got Wyatt Teller, a lot of uh general managers told me that was a good signing. That was really good. I think he fits them. He's going to add some leadership. So, we're going to hear from Wyatt. We'll talk later about Henry Toto. We'll hear some of his interview from the other day before he signed his two-year $17 million contract as a max value. It's a $16 million base value. they decide to go ahead and do it on Henry Toto. No deal imminent for Tommy Tigi. Uh still something that's of interest to both sides, but they went with Henry Toto right now. Doesn't mean that they won't do it. So, Gi deal. And another piece of information uh that I can give you all and this is about the specialist workout they had today which included punishers Trenton Gil and he's previously the Bears, Broncos, Buccaneers, Falcons, Jack Browning previously Buccaneers kickers Chris Freeman and also Will Faren. No immediate signings per sources doesn't mean that they won't revisit it. I think that they might bring in a kicker early in the preseason to give Kaim Fairburn a breather. So, we'll see where that goes. Anyway, right now, without any further ado, we're going to hear from Wyatt Teller. And this is brought to you by my friends at Fence Geeks. Outstanding guys in terms of custom iron work, gates, fences, doors, railings. Check them out at fenceeks.com and on Instagram at fencegeeks. And of course, the great attorneys at PM Law Firm, PMTXLaw.com. You can read all about those guys. They are outstanding personal injury lawyers. If you've been in an accident, give them a call. All right, here comes Wyatt Teller, guys. And then we'll talk more about Henry Toto's extension and a couple of other news and notes. All right, here we go. Wyatt, what's it been like so far? You've been in Cleveland for so a long time. Now you're a Texan and looks like you're fitting right in. Yeah. No, it's uh it's been a good transition. Uh weather's a little bit different. Um but you know, a dieh hard fan base. Uh you know, the plays are similar, obviously different verbiage and uh jargon, but at the end of the day, you got to learn it every year. And uh the technique is a little different, but again, you know, you you got to take it in stride and um you know, there's a lot of change, but it's all been good. >> What do you feel like as far as at left guard? Does it feel pretty comfortable to you now? It's I think you were telling us when you first joined the team that punching to your left could be good for you cuz it's a lot of a lot of mileage on that right hand. >> Yeah. Yeah. No, it's uh it's funny. Everything on my left side from your catch hand now hurts. And now now I can kind of even it out and get everything hurt on my right side. So no, all jokes aside, it's it's been good. It's like, you know, if you're going to change technique, I mean complete opposite technique than what we're used to or what I was used to for so long. Um, being able to kind of like start it fresh from a new position is has been nice. We've been talking with the guys a lot about the culture and the mentality and it is a fairly new offensive line. There's some changes that have I think really added some toughness including and some grit adding guys like you and Keelin and a lot of the other guys Braden. In terms of the mentality, what do you guys want to be as an offensive line? >> Yeah. No, I I also feel like it's an easy scapegoat to just blame the past offensive lines here. Like, you know, it's been a really talented offensive line for a long time. Uh, just putting it all together. uh and you know ba basically you know the mentality of you know it's not like they didn't have good players but just trying to change that mentality of run first and then you know basically you know being able to you know make plays look the same and then if we need to get a pass you know we have unbelievable receivers great quarterbacks great running backs so who can get out open so tight ends unbelievable tight ends so you know if we can put it all together I mean it just shows you how potent this offense can be um but I I I think it's a kind of a scapegoat to just blame the offense And I think that they were very talented last past couple years, but being able to kind of take a take another step forward um with this with with this group, it's it's just going to show that, you know, how special this team can be. >> Absolutely. It's just that work life balance you know being able to detach from your work and know entering back into that into that know real life you know you have so many hours of being around um your family developing hobbies know passions you know being who you are you can't give know everything know to this and leave know every everyone who's came with you behind so being able to stay true to you and uh know find a balance that works for you and uh you can help uh help uh motivate and promote both. I think that's the best way to do it. >> Our audience can't see this right now, but you've got a great view of Kott's hair. Is there anything that could motivate you >> maybe next training camp to do that? >> Yeah. >> Really? >> Yeah. [cheering] >> Do we do I know what it is? >> A Super Bowl. >> Let's go. Let's go. >> Bookmark it. I was going to say that's that's your bite right there. Just the thought of having uh Los Angeles a Super Bowl back in SoFi Stadium. Like how much of a taste can you envision what that will look like? >> I'm big on visualization. So >> yeah, >> you know, at night I'm thinking about know the things I want to achieve. Well, we all hope you get there just the same. Miles, thanks so much for joining us. >> Thank you for having me. >> I appreciate it. Cameron with JB Long and Miles Garrett, brought to you by Community America Credit Union.

title: Sean McVay, Braden Fiske & Blake Corum Press Conference Following Training Camp Practice
text: Aaron comes back. Is there a challenge to saying, "Okay, this is where you're going to play or because he's Aaron Donald, you don't worry about >> Well, I think the best part is is that, you know, you focus on the guys that we do have and if that means that he wants to be able to come back in, I think the cool thing is and you know, you guys know Aaron that that have covered him. I mean, he wants to earn everything he gets and he has tremendous respect for the guys that are in that defensive line room. It's been cool to, you know, see him be able to get to know GIF a little bit and, you know, the workout setting. Um, but you know that those are things that you know you have to be able to figure out on the fly. But what we are focusing on is the guys that are here and then if Aaron is a part of it, it's obviously going to add value to our group which is a positive. >> Coach, what's your overall assessment? >> I'll go ahead. I'll come right back to you. >> Coach, what's your overall assessment of what you've seen in training camp? >> I think it's been good. You know, I mean, I think you take it a day at a time. Yesterday, I thought was probably just overall there was some good moments for each side, but it was probably our, you know, I think it was not a good practice for us. you know, I thought we are better than what yesterday was and I thought the guys came out with the intentionality and you know, the day before that before we took a little bit of a break, I thought it was a really good day. So, humility is only a day away in this league. Um, you know, I do like the way that these guys respond to whatever occurs and I like how we're just being present. Um, but so far so good. Uh, yesterday was a good learning op and I thought today they responded in a better way. I might have missed your answer to this, but is there a specific like benchmark that Aaron Donald has told you like if I can do XYZ, I'm going to be ready to come back. Like is there a specific measure? >> Oh, yeah. There's things that that he has. You know, I don't know that it would be anything that I could specifically articulate, but he kind of knows. I think, you know, when you understand yourself in a in a certain domain as well as he does, he's earned the right to be able to know what he feels like uh physically, mentally, and emotionally to be able to go through the rigors of what an NFL season entails and and do it the way that he's accustomed to. And his standards are different than others, you know, and and he's earned the right for that. So, I think I think he'd be the one that's better equipped to to explain that. I understand and what he means by it, but but he would be the one that would be better able to answer that. >> Couple more guys. Coach, I know asking I know your responsibility is having a macro bird view of the team. I know asking you this question is like asking you to pick your favorite kid, but are there any players that have like been exceptional that have just like sto stood out to you? Uh >> you just answered it. I'm not going to you know there's there's there's so many guys and and I've been really pleased with the collective and I think how how are we coming together as a team? How are we playing 11 as one? Um I've loved the way that the new guys have come in and gotten familiar with the guys that have been here. Um, but you you kind of answered it with the question. It'd be hard for me to point out. I'm uh I feel very fortunate to coach this group. >> Have you finalized plans for when you guys are going to leave to for Australia and how you're going to handle that trip? >> Yeah, but I'd rather just kind of keep it in house. >> What? Why? >> Because it doesn't What's the reason to talk about it, you know? Like I honestly I would respectfully just say, "Yeah, we have, but I'd prefer not to talk about it." >> Is it a strategic thing? I mean, >> I just don't want to talk about it, you know. I [cheering] I don't what does it matter? >> Well, a lot fans I think are curious. You guys fans won't be there long enough for the fans to really have any curiosity about. >> You guys have taken different ways of doing it compared to a lot of NFL teams. Last year you went to London, very short turnaround, played very well against the Jaguars. This is a longer trip. And are you going to do something similar or are you going to give yourself more runway? >> Yeah, I'd rather not talk about it. Coach, coach, does this training camp feel different coming into it? You guys are all in. Super Bowl's here. I mean, might be a last year for some of you. Does this feel any different than the previous training camp? >> No, it's it's a it's a great opportunity to be able to learn and come together as a team. All right. >> Kind of almost >> Yeah. No, I think we're feeling great. You know, I think uh we've put together, you know, I think what practice seven or eight that we've been here and uh you know, I think we've done a really good job stacking days. was competitive football on both sides of the ball and uh you know I think we've made each other a lot better in the days we've been here and you know now we get to go back and sweat in Wooden Hills for a little bit >> now that you guys have had miles out here back out here I should say what are some things you you know learned about each other you know just learning how to rush off of one another and things like that >> uh yeah I mean not all men are created equal that's for sure uh he he's a baller no doubt uh but yeah you know just he's he's getting a slide there ain't no doubt about that so yeah just you know trying to work off him or vice versa just communicating Kayen, I think that's the biggest thing right now is just working our communication of, you know, how to rush together, you know, how we're going to, you know, attack certain looks and, uh, just as all four, the certain looks that we're going to get when he's on the field is just preparing for that and, you know, doing our best to work off each other and, uh, yeah, it's been good so far, though. I think we're we're we're making strides. >> Similarly, what's it like to to rush with some of the new additions in the secondary and how that group's come along with Trevy and Jaylen Watson and knowing their ability to break on the ball when you can rush the >> Yeah. And though I mean it's been awesome and just having that mindset up front of knowing you know you know who you have on the back end that's covering you and uh yeah I think you know just as we continue to marry our rushing coverage as we go forward is just you know continue to build on that and uh yeah you know I think we've made you know great strides through this camp and you know there's still a long way to go you know we still got some joint practices and to get different looks and you know it get a little tire tiring going against the same guys every day and uh but you know still got to build on what we're doing and you know I think we're headed in the right direction. A >> lot to talk about Aaron Donald possibly coming back. you're a guy that would be impacted by that. What's your thoughts on on that possibility? >> Uh yeah, you know, I you know, I try to think of being impacted in the right way, you know, in a healthy way of, you know, a lot I can learn from him if he does choose that way. And if he doesn't, you know, I love the group that we have and, you know, we're getting some really good work out here. But yeah, you know, if that's what he chooses to do, hey, you know, we're here. We're going to get some work. And if he's not, we're going to continue this train rolling and get this thing going. >> Brandon, how do you know when your defense is special? Is there a point in the season or training camp you can tell as a player that this is a unique defense in a sense or one you've never played with? >> Yeah, I mean you always have to wait until you get that first competition, but you can tell you there's, you know, there's little tells in camp of just the energy, the vibe guys bring and just the camaraderie that's built, you know, through these days of camp when you spend all day every day with each other, you know, around the dorms, just around the facilities, you know, when we're in this, you know, confined space. But yeah, you know, I I it's it's a special group. I can say that now for sure that you know we're we're headed in the right direction and like I you know I said earlier there's still a lot of work and there's still a lot of you know that we've got to do to you know continue to grow but I do this group really is awesome and you know I'm ready to just continue to build on that and u yeah you know it's just got to keep on working that's you know end of the day just keep working >> quick and easy [laughter] >> thanks >> feeling great uh camp was good a good uh last day and u I'm super excited for the next practice How does the running back room feel? Is it different this year? What's different about it? >> You know, I feel like every year I've been here, uh, our relationships, that brotherhood, um, just the culture of the running back room has grown and you can really feel it. Uh, I feel like our relationships on and off the field have grown. Whether it be Kiran and I, whether it be, you know, Ronnie and I, Jarz, Jordan, [clears throat] you name it, our relationship has grown. And so, um, I would say, uh, that's the biggest, you know, difference improvement, and it's it's a blessing. I love it. Coach Ron G does a wonderful job at, um, you know, making sure, you know, uh, we're brothers, and it's not just about football, but we can talk to each other about life and so forth. >> Who's the best golfer in the group? >> Oh, Ronnie by far. I feel like, uh, Ronnie Rivers is good at anything. You know, fishing, he's a heck of a fisher. you know, you put him on the golf course. He's a heck of a golfer. One of the top golfers on the team. He's He's pretty good at uh a lot of things outside of football. >> Outside of football, are you guys all pretty competitive? >> Oh, no doubt. >> Um but the cool thing is like when we do our golf outing after OTAAS every year, uh we're always on a team and so, you know, we love competing as a team against, you know, the tight ends, uh you know, the O line, whoever it may be, the defense. And so, you know, uh, obviously we like competing against each other, but when we can compete as one group against others, we love it even more. >> What position group is best at golf? >> I mean, I mean, probably the quarterbacks, I would I would guess. You know, I feel like quarterbacks are always great at golf. You know, Matthew, um, Steady, you know, uh, I don't know how good Tai is, but um, you know, I feel like quarterbacks are always good, but not going to lie, man. Um, we we took I think second, third place in uh the golf outing that we had and uh we each played a part. You know, obviously Ronnie carried us when we needed to be carried, but uh you know, we each uh had some good holes. It was pretty impressive. >> Speaking of go ahead. >> Third third year is usually a pivotal year for for most players. They sort of come into their own. Do you feel that for yourself? A sense of coming into this camp that [cheering] this could be a breakout sort of big year for you personally? >> Yeah. Yeah, I do. Um, you know, I feel more uh calm, cool, and collected. Um, but but to be honest, man, um, I'm just trying to get better each and every day. You know, that's that's where my mindset is right now. Um, you know, there's a lot I can learn from from just just camp in general. And so, you know, obviously I want to have a great year. Uh, I'm always going to put the team first, whatever I can do to help the team. But, you know, uh, you know, I think it's going to be a great year for me. Um, but, you know, I'm just focused on, you know, how much better can I get? you know, what can I improve on? And, you know, that's my my main goal going into the season is just improving each and every day and chasing greatness. >> Speaking of improvement, you were pretty intentional about some of the offseason workouts and exercises you were doing. How do you see that translate or how have you seen that translate on the practice field these last couple weeks? >> Yeah. Yeah. My offseason training, I had the chance to go back home and and train with the trainer, Kevin Johnson, that I trained with growing up as a kid. and um you know his whole philosophy was working the nervous system uh training without shoes on uh working your fast twitch muscles and creating the stiff ankle. So, you know, I feel like uh when you apply that to the field, especially at the running back position, it allows me creating that stiff ankle and that fast twitch allows me to, you know, plant, cut, burst, you know, quicker than, you know, I have before. And so, I definitely think, you know, I've seen, you know, how my training this offseason has translate translated in terms of, you know, that fast twitch and creating that stiff ankle, you know, faster cuts. And so, you know, I'm just going to continue to work on it, um, and be the best version of myself, you know, that I can this year. Like how would you say that uh your relationship with Kyum has grown kind of in your first couple years, but especially this off season? >> Oh, man. It's uh like that's my brother, man. Um like like I was just saying, you know, as a running back group in general, we've grown, you know, every year that I've been here. But I feel like, you know, Kairen and I like that's that's truly my brother. Um I can go to him and ask him anything, whether it be on the field, off the field, you know, he knows he can call me for whatever situation and I'll show up for him. And so, you know, it's really like uh when I when I mean brotherhood, it's like, you know, I really have have love for him. You know, I love uh you know, I don't show anyone my daughter, but you know, I like showing him. Hey, look at my daughter right here. And, you know, you can tell he enjoys it and and it means a lot to me. So, you know, I uh have a lot of love for Kairen. You know, I've learned a lot from him in my years, you know, here. And uh you know, we're only going to continue to grow uh and and be true brothers. Yeah. Co coach had said that coach had said that uh a few few days ago that he felt that Stson when he's out there, you know, is developing ownership of offense when he's when he's out there. How have you seen that his growth, you know, being in a similar trajectory, you know? >> Yeah. I mean, when you look at Stson STSON, >> you can see he carries a certain type of aura, swag, uh when he when he inserts the field, he's not scared to cut it loose. Um he goes out there with with utmost confidence and and his form is beautiful and like you said uh you know coach has seen it, us players have seen it. You know him taking just a a leap in being a field general, taking total command of the offense and you can hear it in the huddle when he's calling the plays. You know he's saying it with authority and u you know I [cheering] mean you guys have seen it. He's he's bought out this camp and he's only going to continue to get better. You know it's a great thing to see. >> Do you think that's elevated guys last year? >> I think so. I mean to be honest, I mean uh when Stson has always had when he's gotten his opportunity, he's always showed up. You know what I'm saying? Since I've been here every preseason game, I feel like he's balled out. You know what I'm saying? And that's all you can ask. You know, when someone gets opportunity, you go out there and show what you can do. And you know, Stson has always done that. And uh you know, I think we all can see it. But you know, he's just one of those guys that continues to get better. You know, he focuses on the day at hand, the goal at hand, the task at hand. And um you know, he makes the most of his opportunity. Blake, Blake, you already mentioned the offseason workouts working with Kevin, how it's increase [cheering] your fast twitch and ankle stiffness. It's translated uh disc. It looks like you're running with more body control, more balance, [cheering] your your the birth of your daughter, how is that bringing more balance to you away from the game? >> Yeah, 100%. I'm just getting chills thinking about it, but you know, the birth the birth of my daughter, you know, means the world to me, man. Um just my perspective on life has changed, right? Like what comes first? Um, you know, it's always going to be God first for me, but after after that, then it's family and then it's ball. And so, you know, every time I step on this field, you know, it's it's never about me. It's always about, you know, who I'm doing it for. You know, my daughter, my wife, my family, my teammates. And so, you know, it's only made me want to go harder. Um, I never thought I was the type of person that that needed extra drive. You know, I've always wanted to chase whatever type of success I'm trying to chase, you know, and I'm nowhere near where I want to be, but I'm going to keep chasing it every day. But, you know, my daughter has given me that extra fire that I didn't even think I needed, right? And so, just the determination that I have now um is through the moon and and it's because of her, you know, and uh you know, whether I have a good day, bad day on the field, off the field, man, like she's here today and uh you know, she just lights up my room and so you know uh I could have the worst day possible, but I know when I get to talk to her, go home to her, you know, she going to put a smile on my face. So, man, it's a blessing. I'm blessed that God gave me such a beautiful uh daughter. like is there a particular area you wanted [cheering] to improve on coming into this season? >> A particular area area. Uh for me, man, um to be honest, I just want to improve in all aspects. Uh I just want to be better. I just want to be I just want to be a better player, whether it be running the ball, pass, catching the ball. But if I had to pick one, obviously uh probably catching the ball. I know I had some drops last year, so I focused on that. Um I feel like, you know, I've shown that throughout camp. Um, but you know, to be honest, I'm I'm the type of guy that I just want to uh I talk to coach G a lot and you know, I just want to chase greatness, whatever that means. And to me, that just means showing up every day and trying to get 1% better. And I think that's uh the special thing about our culture here at the Rams, man. Like, we don't think too far ahead. Uh, you know, we think about the task at hand and each day, like how can we become better football players? And that's I feel like what coach McVey, you know, says each and every day is like, let's get better. Let's get better. Let's get better. Let's get better. Let's not think too far ahead. So, for me, I'm just trying to get better. >> All right. Thanks, guys. Appreciate it. >> Thanks,

title: Inside Vikings Training Camp: Position Battles, Impressions of Offense, Young Defensive Talent
text: Coming up on this episode of Inside [music] Vikings Training Camp, Paul Allen joins us in studio to give us his impressions of camp [music] so far. Plus, we'll hear from players like Jordan Addison and Andrew Van Ginkle. We'll also go in the trenches and discuss the Vikings [music] defensive line battle that's heating up with talent. But first, let's hear from the head coach. >> Uh, you know, I'm a fan of how we handle uh not only the off seasonasons, but the ramp up, acclamation period, all those things. But it's been a long time since a lot of these guys uh as you look at guy to guy on our on our on our roster, especially some of these young guys since they've worn pads. So to uh to have a a physical day where you know we came out uh you know pretty clean across the board from an injury standpoint. >> The Vikings wrapped up their second fully padded practice as practice number seven just concluded. We are inside TCO studios for Inside Vikings training camp. I'm your host, Tatum Everett, and Paul Allen, voice of the Vikings. We're here inside TCO Studios, which must must mean that football is back. >> No doubt. Thank you very much for having me. And uh I'm getting quite excited for the preseason games with the team going in pads, the rubber starting to meet the road in certain spots, and people like you and I get excited. >> Yeah, it'll be here before you know it. And each and every week, we're going to bring you one of these episodes just to get you primed and ready to go for the 2026 season. You've been out here at training camp, Paul. You've had your conversations, seen the practices. What's your bird's eyee overall impression so far? >> Uh, yeah. I think the the the 10,000 ft view because you know granted you know we're close to the team and you know we know a lot of the inner workings with the coaches and the players from last year stuff like that but it changes so much year to year >> and just to see the bevy of new talent they have not only from a rookie standpoint but you know even with some of the free agents with whom they dabbled and college free agents and things like that. Uh there's a lot of competition and even for practice squad spots, you got people just really really going all out. So culture's good, work ethic's really good. Let's get to that Giants preseason game, then let's get to Green Bay. >> Yeah, that that couldn't be more true because when you think of how Kevin Oonnell and Nolan Teasley have formed their staff this off season, they've really focused on player development and these young guys. And I think that that's that is so evident in a lot of the moves that they made this off season. >> Excellent point. One of those guys that we are really excited to see this season is receiver Jordan Addison. [music] And he spoke earlier this week about what the offense is capable of this season. >> I feel like the sky's is the limit for us as long as we just take care of the ball and just don't have no self-inflicted wounds or penalties. You know, we got a lot of playmakers on the offensive side and we got to just help oursel out by not, you know, shooting oursel in the foot. Now, Vikings head coach Kevin Oonnell did address the media on Wednesday about Jordan Addison having a thumb injury, a minor injury, and they don't expect for it to sideline him for very long. Now, Paul, back to these offensive impressions. I want to know what have you seen so far, and what are you excited about that side of the ball? >> Well, that they they have found a way with the player development, uh, which would be the rookies and then a free agent like Jawan Jennings. Then of course you have Kyler Murray and JJ McCarthy. But they found a way to strike the balance between a high-end amount of speed with Jefferson, Addison, uh Aaron Jones, De Man Clayborn. It just goes on and on. They have a lot of speed. Ty Felton too is really fast. >> But they have a lot of physicality in that. Let's not forget because he missed some games last year how physical Christian Darasaw is. O'Neal's physical by nature. or so is Donovan Jackson. Blake Brandle can be physical when moving forward. Likewise for Will Fry. Joan Jennings is one of the best run blocking wide receivers in the last 20 years of football, but he also can catch nine touchdowns. So, they've really found a way to strike a balance of physicality. So, we can beat you this way by by pounding on you, but if you if you flood it and you come up to stop this style of offense, we got a lot of speed around here, too. So, we might go over the top. And uh if and or when Kyler Murray plays, uh he some of his running is absolutely breathtaking there. There are some breathtakingly wonderful sprints that he takes part in during plays when he's eluding pressure. So, their speed, it's all over the place. >> I love what you said about the physicality because up front, their focus right now is making sure they end up on the other side of the line of scrimmage. And I think that that's such a big part of what new offensive line coach Keith Carter has been trying to get these guys to be more physical in the trenches. You can just feel it at camp when you see the ones uh go against the defensive line, which we'll get to in just a second. And I think that's just so impressive. And speaking of the defensive side of things, Andrew Van Giggal is back healthy and we are so excited to see what he's going to do this season. And it was funny the other day, actually earlier this week, he talked about how he's one of the older guys in the locker room. Check out what he said. >> You know, I'm kind of the old guy of the room now. We got a lot of It's It's crazy me saying that, but uh just years of experience, you know, I see the game from a different light than a lot of these young guys. And um they're always constantly asking me questions, you know, trying to uh get a feel for certain situations, different down and distance, what personnel they're in, what there's just so many things that go into it. And um you know, I love it when these guys come to me with questions and um you know, they're just they're so eager to learn and to get better and to grow and um you know, it's going to be so much fun watching them fly around. >> Andrew Vaninkle is going into his eighth season in the NFL, third with the Vikings. And it's expected to lead a defensive or outside linebacker group that has lost Jonathan Grard. And and as he said in his press conference, he's a more of a quiet guy and you know they're going to blitz. So he's kind of leading by example in this. What have your impressions been about how the defense has formed with so many young names now? >> Well, here comes the gink and last year with the neck injury that he had and he missed some games and you know if you are under the belief that even when he was playing near the end, you know, it probably wasn't exactly where it should be were he completely healthy. Andrew Van Ginkle is one of the sneakiest football players in the entire National Football League. In fact, recently on my radio show, 9 to Noon on KFAN, the flagship for the Vikings, Jimmy Sephilo, who played seven years for the Dolphins, he's their play-by-play voice. I asked him about like what was the reaction when Andrew Vaninko left and he was like, "We were devastated." Everybody was devastated. I mean, they've had some cap problems with Miami, so he had to leave, but they felt the impact there crescendoing. We got the crescendo his first year in that game against the Giants against Daniel Jones when he jumped a route, got into the end zone. Now Van Ginkle is on the quieter side, but with Grenard gone, Harrison Smith not here, the there's such an opportunity for leadership that doesn't have to be going up and down the bench and screaming at people and telling them to be better. Leadership comes different ways. Andrew is a born leader. Uh you can blitz him. He's really good against the run. rarely if ever makes mistakes because he's a scholar of the game, picks off passes, gets to the end zone. Now, a big key here is the other guy, Dallas Turner. Because with respect to Dallas, who hasn't done it as long as some others, I envision offensive teams not really paying as much attention to Dallas as they do some other people until he says, "You better double me or you got problems and I'll wreck the game." That has to happen. Then you get in the interior of the defensive line, which we'll get to in a little bit. I mean, if they rush the quarterback from the middle and Turner starts the way he finished last year and Van Ginkle's healthy. Woohoo. I mean, this defense finished as one of the best defenses in the NFL last year. It's going to start the season as one of the best. Van Ginkle has a lot to do with it. We've had several national experts visit Vikings training camp in the first, you know, week or so. And all of them are very high on this defense, expecting much of the same as last year. A lot of that does have to do with the return of Brian Flores, but a lot of it has to do with the promise of what's to come. So, let's get to that defensive line we keep teasing and take a look at the youth movement. We have some vets in the rooms. Their names are Jaylen Redmond and Levi Drake Rodriguez, but these guys have only really been around for two, three seasons. Elijah Williams is a name that popped up last year, respectively. There's a lot of uh expectations that surround three other names in particular, Tyne Ingram Dawkins from last year's draft class, and the first and third round pick from this year's draft class, Caleb Banks and Dominique Orange. Now, PA, I love you picked this group. This group is not only such an important piece of this Flores defense, but they're also a really fun group to talk about and fun guys to be around. They have such great personalities. Uh why did you want to elaborate on them in particular today? Well, for for those who have watched NFC North football for say the last five to 10 years, when the pads went on recently on Monday and Caleb Banks was out there and or recently whatever the day was and I'm looking at him through the binoculars from the Vikings perch where I'm memorizing numbers and stuff and I'm like that's a Keem Hicks. So he reminded me immediately of former Bears defensive tackle Hakee Hicks who wrecked games every single week. So you start there. Now, I think Caleb is faster and twitchier than Akeem, but then you get out on the field and you you watch Caleb Banks when he's singled and the moves he has and and slowly everybody's starting to forget about the foot at Florida, the foot at the combine, and he looks completely 10 of 10. I mean, Caleb Banks has looked so good to this stage, it it causes me to hearken to '09 when I first saw Percy Harvin as a rookie and 2015 when Stefon Diggs was doing the same thing as a deep pick. Caleb Banks is doing some wonderful things. Now, uh the the the the key here is with Redmond and Tai Ingram Dawkins is having a fantastic training camp. It's his second year. title: TE Will Kacmarek & ILB Kyle Louis meets with the media | Miami Dolphins
text: What's it like being in a tight end room where you have guys that have like strengths but then also there is kind of that overlap and how you guys can kind of fit together within that room? >> Mhm. Yeah, um I think our tight ends room is very diverse. Um there's uh some guys that excel in the pass game and there's some guys that excel in the run blocking game. But I don't think anybody can do anything or one thing in our in our room. Like we could all block, we could all run routes and catch. Um and I think we learn a lot from each other. Um you know, coming in with uh um Greg um Sims and uh Cole, those older guys that they have a lot of knowledge that, you know, pours on to us which is which is huge to, you know, grasp the playbook and just tips on the field. >> Speaking of uh Ben, I asked him the other day about the first play of practice and you had a pancake block working off the edge. You're talking about running counter and how much you guys want to identify yourself as that power football team. When you guys look at that in the film room, what's the atmosphere like when they they put up a block of yours where you're pancaking a guy and to give you a little bit >> No, definitely. We uh like I said, like our room takes pride in that and when something like that happens, it's it's huge because, you know, it show it shows our identity and what we're trying to accomplish. But it's not it's not always um sunshine and rainbows. Like when something that you didn't do like um feel correctly, it's going to get addressed and it's not always, you know, happy. But when stuff like that happens, it's it's a great time and everyone gets juiced. >> What's coach Ron Burns do in your room? >> I think just um I mean years of experience. He was a former player himself. Same position. Uh I mean we have coach Lynn who's, you know, played in the NFL for a while, been on the Dolphins for Dolphins uh staff for a while. Um I think those two bring a lot of just knowledge and, you know, emphasis of what we're trying to get done. Whether that's toughness and just making plays when your number's called. >> What's the best advice you've gotten from a veteran about NFL with the training camp? >> I'd say thing that I probably took to heart the most was you're going to make mistakes. It says whether you can make less mistakes than the guys across from you. No one's going to be perfect. It's just about you know getting more consistent. And like I said, winning more than the guy across from you. >> Walk us through like with the first few day seven. How was the first seven days of training camp? >> First seven days of training camp just looking over the people that's older than me, the vets in the room, the people that's already doing what I aspire to be. You know, Jordan Brooks being in the top 67 in the NFL, being in my position group and seeing how he move, how he go through his day-to-day routine, our leadership from T Dot, and then you know, obviously with Jay Rod and Trey just getting close with them as our rookie class. >> Yeah, kind of sometimes with the first couple of weeks you hear about how team needs to have a plan to maximize that. Kind of how's it feel from being the first week to kind of get a feel for all of the ways that they envision you fitting into what they want to do? >> Uh basically what I get is just stay ready. Uh especially with uh coach Joe B, with the rotation he got going on like any down, any snap, my name could be called and I could be out there. Um they got me doing a lot of things, so I'm just basically staying ready to as soon as I go out there to be played in coverage or blitzing anywhere. >> I saw you out there with the guys first few days with Jay Rod and Jay B. Just what was it like kind of being being in the huddle with them and kind of getting a feel for what the future holds? >> Uh it felt good. Yeah, just it felt good to be out there. It felt good to be out there with anybody on the team to be honest. Like obviously it felt good being out there Jay Rod could have seen your both. So like just keep going. Be out there with Jay B. Um just playing off him, leveling up my own ability, just seeing how he move, and just being out there with any other body else that's in a linebacker group feel good because any chance I get to keep getting better. >> What is it like to be on the field with the the NFL's leading tackler >> Leading tackler? Um, on the field I don't really cuz I'm trying to do my job, but I get in that film room I'll be just seeing seeing him shooting through gaps, seeing him make plays, and I'm like, all right, I'mma do that next practice. So, just like I said, just taking notes off him just keep getting me better as well. >> Have you been able to do that? Is it Is it that simple? See it and do it? >> Um No, it's trial and error. Sometimes like I do go out there and do it, but that's the NFL. Uh, the offensive linemen is learning me just like how I'm learning them, so it's all like just trial and error. So, even though I'm keep getting better, the people in front of me getting better as well. Everybody just adjusting. Iron sharpens iron. >> With so many positions on defense and also seeing you out there on special teams doing a whole bunch of stuff, do you try to separate your preparation for the different spots, or do you compartmentalize it all together? Like, how do you how do you prepare for everything that guy's doing? >> In terms of special teams or >> All of it. All of it. Like, do you do you separate your preparation, or is it kind of holistic for you? >> I just go out here ball, man. I don't know how else to say it. Like, I just got to stay ready and go out there and ball. Obviously, the way my career is going to turn up is because I'm an athletic player and I could do so many things, and I just got to showcase the coach. I got to always prove myself on what I could do. So, every time I come out here, I got that chip on my shoulder to prove myself.

The following week, you're going to be going against a new team. title: Jon Gruden on Joining Rondé Barber in the Booth | Press Conference | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: I put my hat on here so I looked apart. I'd just like to say thanks to the Buccaneers for letting me back in the booth and back in the stadium. I'm fired up. We got a great young team here. We've added some players and to be up there with Ronda Barber for three and a half hours. God knows what's going to happen, but we're going to have fun. We're going to celebrate the Bucks and hopefully uh kick off what's going to be a real special season. But I'll be happy to answer any questions. I'm a lot older now. I see Straoud. Uh, he's a lot. He's really old now. But, uh, any questions I can answer. I'll do my best. >> John, we've heard playbyplay. [snorts] >> I've heard I'm doing playbyplay, but I don't know if we if we've solved anything. It's going to be Rond's show. He's the star. I'm just um going to have a production meeting, I know, on August 17th and we're going to finalize the cadence. Um, but I'm excited. I'm a little bit nervous and uh, as always, really fired up for football season, especially Buccaneers. >> Take us a little bit behind the scenes as far as what was your initial reaction when you heard the news that you were going to be able to get back in the booth? >> Well, I was fired up. I had a lot of fun doing it for nine years. I was very fortunate on Monday Night Football, especially the years with Tariq. Uh, we had a lot of fun and we took it every we took every game like it was a Super Bowl. We we took it very seriously, had a lot of fun. So, I enjoy the profession and um at this point in my life, I still study football all the time. I'm still a big fan of the Bucks. I live right down the street, so I'm I'm really excited about it. >> What did you miss about being in the >> I missed um I missed the camaraderie, honestly. I used to go on the road looking forward to seeing our team. We had a producer, a director, we had all kind of cameramen. We had a great team. I I miss that team, that camaraderie, and I really didn't I miss not having to go home after a loss. You know, it's not like we lost any games, but uh we had a lot of fun and I got to learn a lot and see a lot and um I think it helped me in the big picture. >> John, as an offensive guru, what are your thoughts on Zack Robinson coming over from Atlanta to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers? He's got some familiarity with the division. What have you seen from his offense and how he can help Tampa Bay? >> Well, I'm not a guru. I've been fired quite a bit, but uh you know, Robinson, he he comes off of that McVey tree. Sean was here with us in Tampa, as you know. But when you watch him, you see a lot of 12 personnel, two tight ends. Tampa's been a team that doesn't use a lot of double tight end sets. I see a lot of shotgun operation, pistol formation. Uh I I know Kurt Cousins well. I've learned a little bit about their system when he was in Atlanta. I know the terminology is similar to what they had here with Liam and I'm sure that's helpful to the veteran players, but everybody's got to put their own spin on things and u we got to address uh uh the health of our team. We just got to stay healthy and put everything together. But I'm confident that Zach will do a great job. >> You told that, hey, why not play by you told hey why not play by play? You're a broadcasting agent. So, who were some playbyplay guys when you grew up that you admired? >> Well, I I used to imitate a lot of these guys, Lindseay Nelson and Vince Skully and Kirk Gouty. My favorite playby-play guy all time was Frank Gford. You know, a lot of people thought Frank was the color guy. You know, Frank, he was the playby-play guy, that old Monday Night Football Anthem. I used to look forward to the games. And uh Frank, I got to know a little bit during my days at Monday Night Football. He he was clearly my my favorite guy. >> John, what do you expect to see from Baker Mayfield this year? >> I expect to see a lot. You know, he's one of the more productive guys the last three years. If you're into touchdowns and yards passing, uh the durability is what I love about this guy. 51 straight starts. He doesn't complain about the injuries. He plays through things. Hopefully, we can protect them and hopefully uh we take better care of the ball. He has had some interceptions and fumbles. He is reckless, man. But he is fun to watch. I wish I'd have had that guy. >> Yeah. >> Hell yeah. Oh, yeah. I can't even let you finish your sentence. You know, when I was doing the draft at Bartool, I was shocked he got drafted where he did. You know, people are all interested and hung up with arm length and stupidity to be honest with you. If you like James Harrison, you like this guy. He's uh got tremendous effort. That's the one thing that Simeon Rice and Sap, those guys that played with their hand down, did for us. They played every week and they played their butt off in this heat. And we got three games in a in a row, I think, at home to start the season. You watch this guy, he will stand out how hard he plays in the fourth quarter. He doesn't wear down. He's relentless. And that's what the Buccaneers, I think, saw the most. >> John, there are a couple guys with contact disputes right now. What's the key to not let >> Hell I got a contract dispute. I don't really want to talk about the contract disputes, you know. That's for that's for the big boys, you know. That's for uh Jason Light and they'll figure it out. You know, they'll figure it out. >> How do you keep that from like spreading the locker room? You know, guys, do you do anything? >> We try not to, you know, we not try not to deal in everybody's personal contract situation. You got to go out there. This is a dayto-day deal, man. You better string good days together. And I'm confident Mayfield, Vita, those guys are going to do that. They're pros, man. And this thing will all work itself out, I'm sure. >> Social media is taking over. As you know, you got a huge following on social media now. >> Follow you following me? >> Absolutely. [laughter] Either be a coach or eventually get broadcast, >> you know. Uh I'm just thankful to Port Noi for giving me a job. by I love football. Always have. I I just advise people to go to clinics, get in your car, and go and learn football. Accumulate knowledge 1% 2% every day. Personnel, schemes, offense, defense, kicking game. Um, you got to keep learning and uh try to get access to film, try to sneak out and learn something every day. That's the advice I have. You got to keep laying bricks, but if you uh want to be a coach, you can be one. Look, I I became one and I had basically no success as a player. So, chase your passion, go for it, but try to find a way to get better every day. >> Coach, you got to be in the Raise the Flags documentary that came out this past season. How was that, just take a walk down? >> I loved it. You know, I grew up with the Buccaneers. My dad coached here. You know, Doug Williams was was a guy I used to play catch with. I used to throw the drills here. I almost got James Wilder killed twice with some of the throws I made. But um it was a great documentary. The guys did a hell of a job putting that together. Uh they got a lot of people to make contributions to the video. I didn't like the part where I got fired, but other than that, it was a great great show. >> Mike, what are your thoughts on that line? >> Yeah, that's a challenge. You know, Mike wasn't good. He was great. There's a big difference between good and great. What he did here is no one's ever going to do. I mean, 11 straight years. I was here Galloway did it three straight years and he broke a Buccaneer record. Uh most consecutive 10,000 yard seasons. This guy did it 11 times. He did it on the backside of trips. They isolated him. He won 27 contested touchdowns in the last few years. I got him on a reel. They put him in the slot. He he showcased quickness. Uh, I hated seeing him leave and you won't replace him, but somebody's got to step into those shoes and they might do it by committee. I'm excited to see this Hurst kid. 6'4, he runs 44. Uh, McMillan went healthy. He's hell of a player, man. And I like this Tez Johnson guy. He's interesting. But, um, you know, you don't replace anybody like Mike. That's a once in a-lifetime player. >> What intrigues you most? What are the three things that intrigue you the most about this roster? >> Well, I think when healthy, I think from top to bottom, he can beat anybody and and they've proven that, you know, I think that's number one. They got a lot of talent. They've got some depth now because a lot of kids got to play last year. I think that's big. I think the secondly, the front seven on defense has been rebuilt for a good reason. I think the linebacking core, some added pass rushers, some girth inside. I can't wait to see that. And then the transition from coordinator to coordinator. I don't know how Mayfield has done this. Uh they they seem to have a new coordinator every year. That would be the downside if I was Zach Robinson. You know, you get the job. Problem is Mayfield has a new coordinator next year. So you're either getting a head job or you're you're not going to be here. But um I'm anxious to see the Robinson spin on things. And the ball distribution has always been a big part of the Buck success. So, let's hope Buckyy's healthy and some of these young receivers emerge. >> John, have you done any practice runs with >> Who are you, young man? >> How are you? >> Good. >> Uh, have you done any practice runs with Ronda? >> Well, I had a beer with him. That's about it. You know, if you know Ronda, Ronda is a busy guy. He's in a Hall of Fame. He uh he's at the Hall of Fame right now, but we have had some conversations. We'll have a couple production meetings uh before the game and um I'm excited to be with him again. He's been my favorite player for a long time. >> A lot of playbyplay guys have signature lines, I guess you could say. >> You know, I'm famous for giving Pton Manning the name Sheriff. So, I might just drop some new nicknames out some of our Buck players. I don't know. I don't really know about any signature lines, Groot Grinders, you know, stuff like that. I I love football and I love this time of year. I think in this preseason game, we're going to be talking about the guys that are on the verge of making it in the NFL. And what a thrill that is to walk in there as the head coach and you have 53 guys that made the team and there's six or seven guys that are making it for the first time. A lot of these guys have worked harder than you can imagine. And to be a part of watching those guys in the lights on TV in pressure situations is what fires me up the most. >> All right. >> Thank you. >> All right, guys. Have a great day.

text: On it. >> Coach, it felt like your defensive line was bringing pressure all throughout the day. Just your overall thoughts on them. title: Odell Beckham Jr. on fighting for roster spot: “Yesterday’s touchdown doesn’t win you today’s game”
text: Clearly, a week into camp. >> Probably the same as everybody else. Um you know, you're just going you're just finding ways to keep going. Keep putting in the work and push forward. Um wait. Like I told you before, it's like I kind of had two years off. You know, and that time was spiritually, mentally, emotionally, physically, whatever it was, like I got time to like heal, so I feel good. Um At the end of the day, there's no football shape until you get to like week three, four, like Everybody's tired at week three, week four, players are all So just finding ways to stay on top of all the other things, you know, outside of that. Take care of your body. Rehab, rehab, those kind of things, and I feel good. >> After yesterday, it looked like you you had pretty much your biggest workload so far in camp. And then with with the first team a lot with Jackson, how much for you was it important to kind of stack today off of yesterday and to not slack? >> Um in my room at the hotel, you know, there's absolutely nothing to do. It's a beautiful place here. Uh but nothing to do here. And um a quote that I kind of shared with the team was yesterday's touchdown doesn't win you today's game. And I felt like I came out yesterday and I was like, "I want to have my best day." And I felt like I had a a a good day. Right? Some things to work on and learn from and maybe get better. And I was like, "All right, I want to have an even better day tomorrow." And um I feel like the whole team kind of is carrying that mentality, but personally for me, yeah. It is just about stacking those days. Um just finding ways to build confidence, more confidence uh you know, from within the team uh and myself and the >> Was it a challenge going through the first, let's say like five days where there's just so many receivers, there's a lot of rotating, you don't get many reps, and then maybe you don't get a look? Like what was that like, kind of waiting for that day? >> Uh it it's definitely challenging. Um being the competitor that I am, like it's hard when when really love something and you work really hard at it and you want to perfect your craft and then you feel like you don't get an opportunity, but it just comes with the territory of camp, you know. It almost is better because it's like, all right, we spread it out. Everybody's getting theirs. Like, we're fresh we're fresh everybody's fresh. Uh but at the end of the day there's only one ball and there's a bunch of playmakers on this offensive side. We got one of them who's still prepping to get back. Like, there's there's there's guys everywhere, so uh the ball's going to get shared. It's just like any other job, whatever you get to do. >> What's this like for you though? I'm sure you haven't been in the opportunity or in the position very often in your career where you have to produce to make the team. You know what I mean? >> Yeah. >> So, what what's that like to you? Do you put pressure on yourself? Do you think about that? >> Uh I mean, I kind of like it. I mean, my boy texted me. He's like, this is where you thrive. Like, pressure. When I have pressure, I live for it. Turn it on my finger. And to me, I feel like if it's something that's not like if we were just messing around playing fours, we're playing we're like not playing for $100, like I might lose. But you put the $100 on there and then hypothetically, you know what I'm saying? And like, I'm going to I want to step up, you know, to the bigger the moment. So, um I definitely put pressure on myself to make plays. Um and I This is the conversation I had with coach before I ever came here. He's like, you know, I got a really good relationship with you. I don't want to you come here and then something happens and you can't make the team. I'm like, I can live with me getting up, leaving my home, coming here and giving my best effort. And if it doesn't work out, it doesn't work out. I couldn't live with me feeling like I gave up on myself and I never seen through my dream that I've been chasing since I was 4 years old. Like, I just couldn't live with that. So, uh it is what it is. I'm a whole for competition. I've always been like that. I feel like I rise to the occasion. So, right now I'm just trying to just trying to stay in the bag, you know what I mean? I'm trying going get better each and every day. Uh you know exactly what I got to do to get open and catch the ball. Score and get back to the game that I truly love. Uh and I'm just grateful for that opportunity. >> Do you feel like you've gotten any more or in the last couple days? If the results say it, I mean I'm not sure if you say well I've played the same way the first X number of days. Well, does it come to you or are you playing Do you feel like you're playing better? I feel like I'm getting better. I feel like you know, with repetition, with mistakes unfortunately, I'm one of those people that has to touch the stove to know that it's hot to to not touch it again. So, I learned from my mistake and it's like, all right, that's something that I corrected. So, I definitely feel like I'm getting better. There definitely has been more opportunities. Uh it's just a combination of both, but kind of just fizzle all that out and I'm just like I'm just locked in the moment. I'm truly grateful for like being where my feet are at and then just trying to enjoy that each and every day and and bring the best energy that I can. >> So many people talk about wanting to prove things to others. For you, are you proving something to yourself even if it's the last week or so? >> I I feel like if this comes off selfish as that sounds, sorry, but this is like this is for me. This is to prove to myself, you know? Um it's never really been proved to others, but it's always fun when you can prove it to others. But this is for me. This is for my son. This is like in our household like we never give up. You know what I'm saying? Like no matter what it is, like you going to finish what you started. Uh and and that's kind of all it is to me, you know? I take it as if God's giving me 1 year, then it is what it is, but who knows you know, what it's going to be. I'm just trying to be present each and every day. Um and proving to myself that I I am who I know I am, you know? It's not Everybody likes to talk about the old Is he going to be this, that? I'm like you know, LeBron James used to take off before the free throw line and now if he's taking off with his foot right in front of it, he's still got a different game, but he's still playing at a high level. I believe that I can play at a high level. You know, people like to talk about stats and all these things and I'm like, "The last time I played the Ravens, I had 35 catches and 600 plus yards and four touchdowns. If you double that, that's 70 catches, 1,200 yards, and eight to It's It's a great season. So, it's about how many opportunities you get. Knowing that I'm not may not be getting 10 12 targets, like, what am I going to do with the five or six that I get? How can I help uh you know, all the other receivers and the running backs? And how can I help this team? What can I bring? So, I'm not so much caught up in what my numbers are going to be. Like, I just want to be the best me that I can be. I'm going to get open, create separation, catch the ball, hopefully score a lot, um and have fun. That's really all it is for me. >> Last one. Last one. How much juice do you still get when the crowd goes wild when you touch the ball? >> A lot of juice. It's a lot of love. you know, we've had this conversation before, like, most people don't get a chance to like double back. And you know, this is a place that made me into a man, like, made me into who I am. Like, I have so much love for this organization, this city. I got New York tattooed on my back. You know what I mean? I'm from New Orleans. uh all I ever wanted to do was win a championship for the New York Giants and and just having the opportunity right now to, you know, the end goal in mind, but stack those days. That's all I want to do for this city, this organization, is is bring one home. >> Thanks, Victor. Appreciate it.
