A lot of fun. >> How do you think Romello Hightower has handled the the workload that he's been allowed given the injuries at at that spot? >> Smart young man, you know, he's been able to come out and been able to, you know, always the guy you're like scared to talk about early. You know, and I'm sure for you guys, when you watch him move around in shorts, it's not real football yet. Then you get a chance to watch him in pads, and you get a chance to see his physicality and some of the things that he can do. Um, particularly rushing the passer, you know, setting the edge, doing all things that he's doing. Then you get a chance to see a little bit of versatility out of him. So, you're excited about his learning capacity. You're excited about his ability to go out there and play at a very high level. Um, you're excited about um, the what if when he gets a chance to play with Bosa and some of those other guys like Mychal um, that we got coming back. You know, it's it's it's exciting. You know, he's an exciting young player um, that we had a lot of hopes for. And um, hopefully he can meet them. >> It seems like when you guys drafted him, he would be sort of a classic like speed edge rusher guy, but it seems like he's been used in more ways and you just spoke to his versatility. How much is that part of the equation at this point in training camp to you know he has the speed to do that, but he could also maybe do some other things for >> You know, it was it was fun cuz you just had to talk about those things in the in the draft process and and John Lynch and his staff and all those guys would be able to communicate with those guys at a very high level. And obviously on tape you saw um the designated pass rusher role that you can feel that you were losing potentially um that we lost from the team from the year before so he can come in and fill some of those things. But then there was some some further thoughts, some things that we could possibly do with him whether it be fever backer, whether it be spinner, whatever it is. Um being able to get him out of different roles. And then you got to meet the young man and find out what his learning capacity is. Can he handle those things from a down and down out basis? And he's done a really nice job of handling those things throughout the course of training camp and um you know, that's that's all you really can say, you know, and then getting a chance to let him get physical and do some of those things that we're planning. So he's got to keep growing, keep developing, keep getting better every single day and get ready to play our games. >> You've obviously had to plan against Brock for games in the past, but having been here 10 days or whatever it is, seeing him practice daily and especially the last couple days it seemed like he's really really been locked in. Just what have been your impressions of of what's so challenging >> The Layer King has some uh really intensive intensity and I like the I like that about him. You know, it was it's it's really fun for me when you get a chance to get some of those college periods and you get a chance to go in the back with the offense and you call your play and then you get a chance to just hear him operate. You know, you're you're you're listening to him and you're able to hear him operate and you're able to hear him operate in a very pro manner. Um how he communicates with the coaches, you know, how he's very up front. Um today he got fired up, which was cool. Uh which was fun, which was competitive. Um and and and I love that. And like when he does those things it just makes the team go. You know, I I watched our team go out there and basically have a fight for an hour and a half and then all hug at the end of practice and cheer for each other. It's the weirdest thing ever. It's awesome. But um it was a lot of fun with that guy, you know, he's awesome. >> You have But, returning starters at corner obviously, but you also have Jack Jones, a veteran guy. You kind of know what you're getting from. It seems like he makes a play day out there. Where does he fit in that room? >> You know, we have a highly competitive room. You know, we got to be out there and find out who's going to be our guys going out on every down basis, but you never got enough good players and Jack Jack certainly one of them. You know, he has a chance to go out there and make a play. I mean, he has a chance to go out there every single day. We going to be competing at a very high level right up until the end. I'll let those guys make those decisions on the field. Um you love that. I've always been a part of highly competitive rooms. You want highly competitive rooms. You don't want to be able to come up here and put the depth chart up right now. That probably means you're not that good, so we got a lot of spaces like that and that's fun for me. >> How difficult or easy is it for a cornerback to transition to safety? Like where say you want to have Stout on the field more cuz he's likes to get in there and stick his nose in there and has ball awareness. Like how hard would it be to move him to safety or Price is actually the taller rangy guy? >> You know, I mean, out of the pace and demeanor, Stout can play whatever he wants. You know, Stout can play the linebacker. Stout can play safety. Stout can play corner. You know, right now he is our starting star. He's our starting nickel. And him going out there playing at a very high level with his hand usage, his ability to get up to the pass rush, his ability to pass rush, his ability to use his short space quickness, um defend anything, whether it be zone, whether it be man, um highly competitive young man, um stays angry every single day. I love him. Like he's a He's got the mindset of a football player. He's got the mentality of a football player and he's only has the movement and the skill set of a football player. And then, to just talk about being versatile with guys, I think we kind of did that a little bit. You know, switch the corners with DeMar and Ronaldo, make those guys go opposite, make Jack Jack play opposite. You know, making those guys, you know, whether it be Surtain playing in a little bit of safety, being able to play corner, you're creating versatility across the board cuz you just never know what happened in the game. You know, DeMar playing inside a little bit for us the other day, being able to do some different things for us. You know, when things happen in the game, someone goes out there a course of the game, you want to be able to have an answer. And it's our job as coaches to have an answer for our head coach when something goes wrong, what we're going to do and what our plan is. It may not be the right plan. It may not be the right decision, but you better have one. >> It seems like you're cross-training Dugger a little bit. Where What's the plan for him? >> I think that's kind of the the theme, you know, throughout the the course of training camp. You know, you get in the camp, you put people in positions, you let them grow, you let them learn, you let them get comfortable, and then you find a way as a coach to make them uncomfortable. And then that really breeds understanding, and that that that really lets you know um how these guys are really understanding the whole entirety of the defense, what their brothers are doing, what their people are doing around them. Um you know, this game is played from the neck up. You know, plays are made when, you know, opportunity and technique meet. But if you can just take the opportunity and technique and put it together at that position where you're there and be where you are, be where your feet are, um I think that's the best course of action for our guys. >> Take up more >> it totally wrong, but similar to what I you were just asked, with Jordan Walker, I saw him taking some reps with the defense here at like after the 11-on-11 drills. I don't know exactly what was going on. Is he also being >> That'd be new to me, but you know, I'll take him. >> Could preseason or going up against another team be for somebody like Bryce Young? >> That is huge. Uh So funny, he must have been walking in the hallway with me the other day. Um I was just talking about that, like these rookies, right? You get into training camp and it's like this this moment that they play and they kind of feel like they belong. And you start to feel it in practice, right? The other day we saw him on a couple plays, knocked down pass, get excited, team gets excited for him. And then you you kind of get that sad face off and I belong and like then it's like I can't wait to get to the next practice and be able to go out there and compete, but then you really see it and you get in those competitive moments with people they don't know. And when you get into that practice of whether it be a joint practice next week versus Tennessee or whatever the case may be, but you get to get another one versus LA, or whether it be one of the preseason games, you get a chance to see that step, and you see those guys make those steps, you know, like I just remember some of the young safeties that I coached that gotten to position to make the play and never could make it in practice. And then they get in the game and they just miss it. And then they get in the game and they finally start making them. And then they become guys. And like those are the steps you want to see made by your young rookies. Um it's just a matter of how fast they can do those things before you got to make those decisions on who's on the football team. >> What do you Is there any time during the off season or preseason you think about what Sean McVay is thinking about, what Raheem Morris is thinking about, what Sean McVay >> That would be every day, coach. Um you know, that's constantly going through your mind, right? You you you know you know, being a familiar face in that building and kind of knowing what those guys do, but knowing they're going to bring their very best every single time they go out there. They get better and better every single year. Um you got to be able to go out there and plan for some of that type stuff that along with uh finding out who's going to make your football team. And that time will come. You know, when you sit down in the room and you go plan things and you got to go out there and play that game, which is the most important part of what we do. Um but that time will come. But it's definitely time to do those things. You always think about those things. Um you have those moments throughout the course of the summer. Um you have those moments throughout camp. You have those moments as you put in more situational football. And you tie them together and uh create some similarities what you can do when you play those people so you can have carry over for you guys. To make it simple. Thanks, guys. Hello. How we doing? Good. >> Uh talking about Brock and at practice he likes to call him the layer king. >> Mhm. >> Do you call him that as well? >> The layer king? I like that. Kind of like lizard king or something. Uh yeah, Brock does a good job with that. I think Raheem he's had some issues with that in the past. People quarterbacks in the NFL doing that, so maybe he has some scars. >> How do you feel so far about training camp? >> Good. Um I like training camp. I think it's good just to get around all the guys and it's never going to be perfect. I like the season a lot better. It's what I'm really good at is preparing for games and being ready to go in there at any time and training camp is is fun cuz it's a lot of challenges and different unscouted looks and things that you don't normally see, so um I think it's a good challenge and I don't think training camp tells you how your season's going to go, but I think it's good to have mistakes, but also good plays, too, so you can never overreact or underreact to it. Um not that it's not important, but I I really enjoy the games, you know. >> How different is this defense that you're going against from a schematic standpoint? >> Yeah, it's pretty different. Um I played against Raheem last year, you know, as a quarterback and against the Falcons, so kind of familiar with it and what he did in LA, so there's a little bit of everything in that regard and um a lot more match coverage, so the throws are a lot more contested. I'd say that's some teams in the league play that way, but a lot of teams don't now. Um so it's kind of an interesting balance. Um but yeah, it's been a good challenge. They bring a lot of pressure, too. On third down, so it's a little different than what we've been used to, but um I think they're doing a great job over there. I like Raheem's personality. He has a good personality and um I don't know. It seems like a good coach you'd want to play for. >> I know he's missed a couple days here, but with dribbling, is there a just a a combination of size and speed that he has that where you're kind of getting both that that you maybe didn't have in the receiver room even last year or this >> Definitely. Yeah, I call him the flying Hawaiian cuz he's so fast. But, he definitely is fast, but some guys um you know, they can be really quick, but they're not as strong. So, he has both. Um I don't have a comp for him yet, but I don't I think he'll be a really good player. Obviously, um got a chance to throw to him in the off season a little bit like when we went to Nashville and stuff and I don't know, just the way he got to the ball when it's in the air was impressive. He has like a second gear when the ball's in the air. Um some guys are really fast, but when the ball goes up and your eyes go up, you slow down, but he doesn't do that. So, it's pretty impressive and we got a few guys that are like that, Jordan Watkins and obviously Mike Evans is one of the best at it. So, you want to have guys like that and uh speed is good, but you want ball speed where the ball's in the air they don't slow down. So, he has that. >> That was >> You said you like Raheem's personality. What stands out to you about just that personality and just how he or carries himself? >> Um he's awesome. I think he doesn't take the game too seriously. Um I think that's important. Uh obviously, it's a very intense serious game, but you want to also have fun with it and he's going to talk smack and you know, when he gets beat, he kind of just rolls it off his shoulder because he knows there's a next play. So, I really like his personality in meetings. I walk by him every day and talk crap to him and stuff. So, um he's definitely a been head coach and I think he's trying to find his feet, you know, back here and um I feel like he'll he'll be back in the head coaching spot soon. >> How are you adjusting to the other targets in the wide receiver room? Obviously, you have faces out there. You spoke on Shribling, but >> Yeah. >> Um you know, with him being out and Evans also being out the last few days, how are you adjusting to the other guys? >> Yeah, it's been um it's been interesting. I think it's good. I think everyone's kind of a melting pot um of people and we got young guys and old guys and like you said, Christian, Mike, and some and Shribling weren't out there, but it's good for these young guys to step up and make plays and I need to do a better job getting them the ball and letting them uh show what they can do, but I feel like they've all flashed in different ways. Like even Junior Bergen like going out there knowing what to do, playing fast, um all that stuff. So there's a long list of guys so I could go through each one of them, but I've been impressed with their work ethic and our system is complex so I'm not expecting them to to get it in one day or one week or even one month. It takes a whole all the way through the season because our game plans are very different each week and um that's the challenge is being ready for that. >> What have you seen from Jordan Watkins last year compared to this year? I know you worked with him. >> Yeah, um I think I really like Jordan. He's one of my good buddies on the team and he's always got a good attitude. He just goes out there and runs fast and with with us we're very similar because we're hard on ourselves. So like if he has a bad play, I always try to like go up to him and be like, "Hey, play the next play. It's all good." Um similar with me like if I have a bad play, you know, I want him to do the same and we kind of have that relationship so um for him it's just playing that next play as best he can and he's done a better job of that this this training camp and he's really fast and has a lot of talent and has played in a lot of big-time football in college so um you know that he has what it takes to be really good. >> You know, you guys have talked about, you know, not really missing a beat in veteran locker room dealing with not having your head coach, but has it been weird? Like what's it what's it been like for you guys sort of adjusting to what Kyle's been going through and and that whole process? >> Yeah, I think it's it's good. I think it's a good challenge in its own way. I think everything will be fine and great in the long run. Um but nothing's been too different. I feel like this organization is run very smoothly whether Kyle's at the top or somebody else. I think he set it up that way so um really he's been he's been out there. He's been talking to us so I'm you know, hopeful that he can recover all the way and um for us it's just keep battling every day. It's camp. We're kind of getting to that middle part and and then we'll get to the exciting parts playing in the games and stuff, but as a team I feel like the energy is there and like you said, we got a lot of good old guys on this football team. Not old, but older. I guess I'm approaching that area. But, I think it's good. I think you want those guys in this in this season. It's not going to be easy. We're not going to Maybe we don't start great or we do, it doesn't matter, but you want that head leadership to be there and that's Kyle and all the veteran coaches and then all the veteran players that have been through a lot of seasons. >> How different is it having Clay in in your ear during during practice though and then just in terms of not even just the play calls, but like the feedback that you get versus what what you get from Kyle? >> Yeah, it's good. I think Clay like sometimes he mumbles a little bit. So, I'm just trying to hear what he says. But, no, he's amazing. He does a great job and like just getting us ready for practice. Right now, it's just hard cuz like we don't have like an exact call sheet, you know, so it's like you have the whole library of plays and just trying to hear like, "Did he say that? Like is that a play we're going to run?" So, I need to do a better job there. But, like Clay's called a lot of plays, you know, in the preseason and um obviously during the season, too. He's gotten a chance to call some games, so he has really good experience and he's very good coach. He's clear when he stands in front of the the team about what he wants and like today he called us up during practice and the beginning of practice was like, "Hey, he kind of felt like a little bit of an energy low." And Clay was like, "Let's get this going." So, as players like I need to respond better to that, but I think we did overall as a team. Like we made some big plays today, so that was just a good example of like he is good X's and O's, but he's also really good with like how he talks to the team, too. So, you want to have both. >> Are you still hearing Kyle a lot more though, right? Like he's standing closer to the team behind the offense and >> He's inching towards us. >> Yeah, he is. Um wait, what was your question? >> Are you just hearing his voice a lot more, the pointers, you know, after plays and things like that? >> Yeah. Yeah, Kyle's always been involved in say like compared to other teams I've been on just very as a head coach, it's obviously his offense and he understands it all and I think he wants us to take it to the next level of like how can we get this even better? So, he's always voicing things and asking us and not necessarily telling us like asking us, "Hey, can do you think you can get this done?" And we either can or we can't, but that's the whole point of training camp is to try. Um and during the season it's completely different. Like he's in all the meetings and um has a chance to sit down at the at our quarterback room and we go through each play and the problems and all that. So, he does a great job. He's still doing a great job of that. Um just training camp is, like I said, it's more of a widespread net versus like one individual game plan. >> The meetings with you guys yet? >> Uh yeah, he's been he's been around. Um he's doing a good job like like I said, recovering. I don't know. You'd have to ask him how he feels overall, but I feel like he's doing a doing normal Kyle stuff. >> We're getting a a play call that's uh going to be a deep shot, a deep throw. Do you get excited? Does it air it out because obviously the fans that are in attendance saw some today? >> Do you get Do you get that as well and does >> No. >> I don't really get excited. I think like you have to play each play and like during the games and stuff, if you have too high of a pulse, it's sometimes a bad thing and I don't know. Deep balls in practice are fun, but sometimes it's not realistic, I guess. So, you have to just play it as a real play. Like there was one today I had a chance to throw a deep I had to move and then threw an interception. So, it's like that messes up the timing of the play. Um so, you just have to play each play how it is, but my goal is to just try and get it to the right read and yeah, I'd say lower your pulse. Whether it's a screen pass or a Hill Mary. You can't get too excited or not excited because sometimes that puts too much zip on the ball or whatever. Everyone's different, but yeah. >> How much of a difference do you sense with Dre being back there with Fred? >> Oh yeah, definitely definitely feel the the defense and their energy. And you got Raheem yelling random stuff in the background. So, yeah, it's quite the challenge. I don't know if he'll be able to stand on the field on game day, but uh Fred is obviously our our main guy and Dre's been out there, too. And Wallows done a great job and gifts so you got a lot of veteran guys that played a lot of football but I think those are definitely the energy makers over there. Um stout too like stout's one of my favorite guys he's he's just he is who he is you know he's not going to change in practice today like he gets chippy and um he wants to just make plays. >> What's the difference in Bernardo Green to play this year? >> Yeah. I do. Um I think Nardo went through some things last year whatever like you want to call it and he's just he's a pro though he came back and he's played his technique really well. He's made a lot of contested plays him and the and the hyena and then Jack Jones too I played with in the past like those guys are all aggressive corners I feel like there's a lot more plays being made on the ball compared to last year which is a good thing um just contested plays so they've done a great job over there and I'm excited to see him in a real game and see what it looks like. >> Is Raheem more vocal in in practices than Robert Saleh was? >> Yeah I think so. Yeah Saleh was pretty chill like he would just stand back there and look all strong and stuff and then >> Raheem like maybe not as strong looking but definitely like a louder voice. Um but yeah they're very similar and schematics are obviously different but they're both great coaches so. All right cool thanks guys. >> How has the different offseason campaign for you now that you've been in it a year? >> Uh different wise? I mean it's the same play calls, same plays, so I wouldn't say it's nothing different, just being able to, you know, showcase a little bit more of my talent. >> More comfortable in it? >> Oh, yeah, yeah, for sure. Being my second year, yeah, I'm definitely more comfortable. >> I know you weren't here last season, but you now have Mike Evans in the room with you and Deebo Samuel. Does the room feel any different this time around than it did last year, and if so, how? >> No, no, it feels the same, you know, guys come in here, guys leave. Uh I think those guys coming in ready to compete, um trying to make plays, trying to help the team win. >> You were one of the few wide receivers who didn't get hurt last year in in the summer, but then you had to serve the suspension. Did you feel like that that kind of interrupted the the flow that you had going on in the summer when you when you came back? >> No, not really. >> You had a different quarterback, I think. I mean, it went from Brock Purdy to Mac Jones. I mean, was that problematic for you at all? >> No, sir. >> Can you take us back to the start of free agency when you had a number last year and you guys signed Mike Evans? How how did that conversation go as far as you relinquishing that number? >> With Mike? Uh he was just asking for number five and I ain't mad at him. He's just a number, so he can he can have it. >> You guys go back pretty far, right? Like >> Who? >> You and Mike Evans. >> I only met Mike this year. >> Okay. Yeah. >> Strong great training camp as far and obviously there's been more opportunities too with some people injured and whatnot. What's your mindset and have you done anything different in the off season approaching this year's training camp? >> No, same thing. Try to get better, come back better than I left last year. Um come back try to help the team win. >> It's like Bernado Green and De'Omar have been excited about the scheme. What have you seen different from those two guys when you're up against them? >> Uh they look a lot more comfortable. Um I say they definitely been playing a little bit better to my eyes. Uh like the like I would say towards their technique as much as so last year. So, I feel like they feel more comfortable. They feel good inside this scheme and to me it look like they well well on point right now. >> Couple plays yesterday in practice today where balls in the air and you're going to the right spot. Like there was there was a throw yesterday Brock probably couldn't see you but he threw to the spot. I mean, how much is that instilled in you as a receiver that you have to hit that landmark and like what kind of details has Kyle kind of emphasized over the last year that you've been here with him? >> I think it's you know, every team you know, you got to get the timing down with the quarterback and sometimes the quarterback is expecting you to be in a spot when he can't see you in that spot. So, he trusts you with to get to that spot um in certain plays and you that's why we go through training camp OTAs and stuff like that just to get that timing in and and route running down so we could be on point. >> And you feel like you got that trust with Brock now over the years? >> I think so. I hope so. >> How did you spend the off season coming into training camp? >> Uh just training um working trying to come back better and faster than I did last year. >> Have you noticed Brock taking any steps or highs in terms of just how precise he is or or anything like that this this >> Uh seems like the same Brock to me. >> Anything else guys? All right, cool. Thank you for your time. >> Appreciate it. >> We're going to have Alfred Collins coming in, too. >> Yeah, I think we have Alfred Collins here. >> [clears throat] [snorts] >> Alfred back, how's it been getting reintegrated into the team and into some of the workouts? >> Uh, it's been awesome. It's been a blessing. It's been a journey, and just to be back on the field with the boys, you know, it's so much fun. I love it, yo. >> What have you sensed different from Ricky Morris versus last year? >> Uh, just the energy he brings. From the first meeting we have, you know, he's just energetic, you know, gets gets us going. Um just uh it's just infectious, you know, and it makes you just want to play harder, so. >> How big of a process did you have to go through to getting the shoulder repaired and just were you anticipating what it was going to be like and then when did you initially hurt it? >> Um you know, I just I knew this off season was going to be huge, you know, just making sure my body's in the best shape it can be for this 18 weeks. Um but now I was just very intentional, you know, listen to the the staff, the strength staff, you know, everybody that helped me, the dietitianists, all that, so. Just want to make sure I was in the best shape as I can to for the season. >> Did you deal with that shoulder a lot your rookie year? >> I mean, you know, it's football, you know, you get nicks and knacks, you know, you got to play through it, so yeah. >> You were able to make huge plays for the 9ers last season and played quite a bit out there with them. When you come into your second year in training camp, what's the difference given that all the experience you got in game time action, what's the difference in training camp rookie year, training camp second year? >> Um I feel like just from going going through training camp last year, you know, I was a little stressed and stuff like that, you know, everything's new, you know, it's intense, but this year, you know, just taking a step every day, not uh being too hard on myself, but being hard on myself, not getting too high, not getting too Oh, Not getting too high, not getting too low, so you know, I feel like that's the biggest difference from last year. >> What are the differences with the adjustments being made to the defense? Um a lot of guys saying, you know, in different ways that the new defense is giving the team energy, excitement, it's fun. How is it for you? >> Um you know, it's just whoop the guy in front of you his butt, you know what I'm saying? Like go attack. Um we got each other's back, you know, we know I know the assignments that Fred and Dre got, you know, so just learn the whole defense. It [snorts] feels like a puzzle piece. Damn, right? >> I'm going to scoop back a little bit more. >> With the microphone. >> Scoop back a little >> Osa and and Grayson Halton are new in your group. What do you see of each guy? How would you describe Osa and how would you describe Grayson? >> Osa, he's a he's a leader in our room, you know, he uh Shoot, me too. Me and myself, you know, and uh everybody, we're just sponges to each other, you know. They see something they give us advice. If I see something you know, and then Grayson, he's just a sponge, man. He's working his butt off, getting better every day, and I'm excited to see what he what he does. >> What are your goals working with a nutritionist over the off season? just eating healthier, like leaning getting lean out, you know, so I can be faster, more explosive. Um just limiting, you know, just eating right. >> So, you're on the field? >> Yes, I do. Yes. >> A good complement to to Osa, just uh that kind of duo that uh you guys will have in the middle this year. >> Uh you said you you said what? >> A complement, like do you do you kind of do different things? Um you know, uh you kind of play off of each other. >> Oh, for sure, you know, that's just going to come with reps and, you know, getting to feel each other's play, you know, and then but I feel like we're going to be something we're going to be we're going to be all right. >> Is your role different in this defense compared to last year? >> Stop the run. Get to the quarterback. Not really. >> Is your position like nose guard, three technique, like that stuff? >> What have you learned from Osa? >> Man, his work ethic is something I've never seen before, so like it inspires me to do more. Like he's been in the league for a while now. He's in here longer than anybody, you know, you know, it's inspiring to me, you know, so I'm picking up picking up what he's doing and even on the field, just his effort and attention to details, you know, it's infectious to me and the and D-line group. >> How have you and CJ felt coming into your second year we're excited we're excited you know it's my dog my hand Bandit you know we ready to recap it. >> You staying in close contact with Michael as well? >> Yeah yeah yeah he's doing good yeah. He's doing great yeah. >> Good day guys. Thanks Alfred.

title: The Good and Not So Good from Day 8 of 49ers Training Camp
text: Here's who stood out on day eight of 49ers training camp. Keep in mind the players have a dragth through tomorrow, so the media will not be in attendance. The good quarterback Brock Perie. He absolutely eviscerated the starting defense today while throwing to wide receivers named Malik Turner and Cadel Hajj. Technically, Pertie's number one receiver on the field is Debo Samuel, but he can't get open. So, Pertie is forced to go through his progressions and fire tight window throws to players who may or may not make the final roster. And despite all this, he threw two deep touchdown passes today and no interceptions. In fact, he's thrown just one interception in all of camp. He's making good quick decisions, and he's playing with the most confidence I've ever seen from him. There's no question that he's having the best camp of his career. Unfortunately for him, his offensive line is shaky. His running game is non-existent, and his receivers mostly are injured. The Niners need to get him some help before he gets injured like last season. Quarterback Diamador Lenor. The Niners don't have a healthy wide receiver who can challenge him. Today, he casually broke up two passes intended for Debo Samuel without trying particularly hard. A few years ago, Samuel would have worked Lenor. Now, Samuel can't even make him sweat. Neither can Demarcus Robinson nor Jordan Watkins. I doubt opposing offenses will target Lenor much this season. There are other defensive backs they can pick on. More on them in a minute. Nickelback Upton Stout. He's so much better than he was last season. Brock Pury almost never targets him because he gives up practically zero separation. Sometimes he gets beaten at the catch point because he's short, but not often. And he's an absolute savage against the run. Today a wide receiver tried to block him and Stout picked him up and threw him on onto his back. This was roughly 60 yards away from me, so I couldn't see which wide receiver Stout pancake. Fortunately for that receiver, Stout is by far this the best secondyear player on the team. The Niners have to find a way to keep him on the field at all times. Quarterback Jack Jones. He undercut and intercepted a deep playaction pass from M. Jones that was intended for Jordan Watkins who was running a deep over route. Jones isn't as good as Lenor or Stout, but he does intercept more passes than them. So, if Jones starts and opposing offenses try to pick on him, he'll burn them eventually. I'm warming up to the idea of him starting simply because he's a playmaker in a secondary that needs one. Free safety Maris Seagull. He does one-on-one drills with the quarterbacks and wide receivers, not the safeties and tight ends. And he actually wins some of his reps, unlike Jier Brown. More on him in a minute. Today, Seagull broke up a pass that was intended for Junior Bergen, who was running an out route during one-on- ones. Seagull is the best safety on the roster, which isn't saying much, but he's improving in coverage, and he's a good tackler. Defensive tackle Grayson Halton. He missed the first week of training camp with the knee bruise, but he has been healthy for the past two days, and he's showing that he's a good interior pass rusher. Today he beat secondyear guard Connor Kby cleanly with a pushpull move. Halton seems like he'll develop into a three-own starter as opposed to Alfred Collins and CJ West who look like two down players. Wide receiver Dejon Stribbling. He returned to practice after missing a few with hamstring tightness but did not participate in one-on- ons or 11on1vens. Instead, he put on his pads, warmed up with the wide receivers, then rehabed with the trainers. At least he's progressing. The not so good defensive end Nick Bosa. He missed his second practice in a row due to soreness. According to the team, that sounds minor and precautionary, which is why it's surprising that Boza hasn't been on the field at all the past two days, not even as a spectator. He has been completely missing an action. Is his knee sore, or has he simply decided to stop practicing? Keep in mind, he hasn't really practiced yet this off seasonason. He's suited up and gone through warm-ups with the other defensive linemen, but he hasn't competed in one-on- ons or 11on1vens, and yet he's injured. makes no sense unless his body is beginning to break down or he believes the electrical substation theory, which I do. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw also missed his second practice in a row due to soreness, but he at least showed up, wore his pads, and took mental reps as opposed to Bosa, who had something better to do apparently. So, good for Green Law. Still, you have to wonder if his body will hold up for an entire season. It didn't last year, which is why the Broncos got rid of him. Wide receiver/runningback Debo Samuel. He's in shape, but he's not fast anymore. And he's still a subpar route runner. But the Niners need to find ways to use him because they have roughly 20 injured players. So today, he played running back and carried the ball three times, which shows you how thin the running back position is right now. The more the Niners have to use Debo Samuel on offense this year, the worse they'll be. He's washed. Jordan Watkins is a better receiver than him. Quarterback Renardo Green, he doesn't intercept passes, so he's the main target for opposing teams when they want to challenge one of the Niners quarterbacks. Worst case scenario for the other team, Green will knock down the pass. Best case scenario, he'll give up the catch or get flagged for pass interference. Today, he got flagged during a one-on-one rep against undrafted rookie Wesley Grimes, who probably won't make the team. Green is in serious danger of losing a starting spot to Jack Jones. Strong safety Gyier Brown. He gave up a long touchdown catch to Malik Turner, who's 30 and probably won't make the team. Meanwhile, Brown thinks he's a top five safety in the NFL. Truthfully, he'd be better off adding weight and moving to outside linebacker. He's going to get picked on all season until he gets benched and replaced by Malak Mustafa if he can ever stay healthy. Quarterback M. Jones, he threw yet another interception, this one to Jack Jones. M. Jones is having a miserable camp. Last year, he arguably played better than Pertie in camp. Jones was locked in. This year, he's not. He needs to get it together fast because the Niners are going to need him to play at some point in the next few months. [music]
